title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. I hear you. [music] I am Heat. Heat. >> [music] >> 4 I can't stop. Now that's Heat. Doo doo doo doo doo doo. Hallelujah. Well, uh, game that I felt like we're comfortable being in, uh, like that at the end and the guys kept fighting, giving us a chance the offense putting together a really good drive in the fourth quarter. Um looking like us and looking like what we expect with the run game, the actions coming off of it and uh being able to move down there and finish in the end zone. On the flip side of it, defense going back out there at the very end once they had scored, you know, but uh giving us one more chance and those big stops, you know, the second down, then they moved back. Then the third and one or sorry, we declined it. Then the third down and the fourth down stop right there with a minute to go. the whole field in front of us, no timeouts. I'm still thinking we got a shot. Our guys are comfortable in this situation and we weren't able to uh pull that off. Again, I got to give credit to the Browns, what Coach Monkin's doing with this group, uh the energy that they played with and you can feel a sense of a toughness and a sense of belief on that team. Um where they just kept battling with us throughout it and um and at the end of the day made it made a couple more plays than we did. There are several reports that JC is going to be placed on IR and has Can you tell us more about the quad injury? >> Uh, I won't get into specifics because there still we're still getting second and third opinions to figure out what that timeline looks like. That'll determine everything for us, but I will say it's a significant quad injury. Um, and uh, we'll just take all that information and and make that decision as we get it. >> Will he be placed on IR for sure? Uh, it looks like that right now, but again, I don't want to say anything definitively um until I know all the information. >> Can you say who was torn? >> Uh, I I don't want to give anything Wednesday. I'll tell you everything about it um and give you the full nature of it. >> Dave, how did that happen? I mean, he I know he was away from the play, but obviously in coverage. >> Yeah, I think it was just a change of direction thing and and also just a you know, just kind of a freak fatigue type of deal. you know, it was a long drive and uh Deshawn was able to extend that play and so we tell our guys to plaster, you know, go match your guy in the area and you got to cover for a long time when a quarterback can do that. So, um I think that was the nature of it. >> Dave, um in the short term, Mike Jackson also suffered a groin injury at the end of last game. >> Um what is the shortterm plan at cornerback right now? >> Yeah, right now Will Lee, uh Caleb Evans stepped in and played some quality snaps for us. Um, I was really pleased to see him do that. Shaw Smith Wade's going to have to hop into the mix. Um, you know, could be possibly Cory Thornton up from the practice squad. Um, again, Dan's looking all around and and making sure that we, you know, uncover every stone to see uh who can come in and help us and preferably somebody who's has some familiarity with our scheme, but at the same time, we're going to be open to options to help us. I mean, when when you're playing a Caleb Evans or Shaw Smith Wade, you in main roles on defense, how hard is that to kind of facilitate the special teams then because of the roles that they play there as well? >> That's right. It all it all, you know, um it affects the whole thing. So, you're right and that's another part that we have to consider. >> Um Damen Lewis finished the game, but in the locker room it seemed like he was kind of struggling with his elbow. What What's the latest on him and what's the latest on Jaylen Coker? >> I'll give you guys all the all the specifics of it. Uh, Doo does have something going on in his elbow. Um, Jaylen felt his quad. We're taking all that stuff. We're doing imaging. We're kind of looking at the full picture to see who who we can get back for this week. Is it going to be longer? We have a by-week coming up as well. So, there's all these things to kind of take into consideration. >> Are JC's um second and third opinions going to be done locally or is he going to a specialist for those? You know, >> I'm assuming it's it's kind of the leading guys out there with this the nature of these types of injuries. Um, how do you feel about the three guys that were ruled out or inactive this past week? Um, Devin Lloyd, Xavier Legette, and Nick Scott. >> Uh, feel really confident that Devin will make it back this week. Um, Xavier, we're going to have to see. We're gonna have to take him dayto day and just to, you know, kind of see where he's at um with the knee. And then, uh, who else did you ask about? >> Nick Scott. >> And Nick Scott was the rib. And so, again, we'll get him moving around out there. Uh, seems to be a playable condition. got to make sure the whole thing fits right and make sure he's ready to go. >> Dave, concerning overall just I mean I I I know I mean the by-week is coming at a really good time for you guys but concerning with the with the amount of injuries. >> Absolutely. I mean this is you know leaguewide this is to be expected in the first four weeks. This is a lot on one team and I can't really put my finger on it. But um all of us, all the the directors of every department, we're all putting our heads together. We got a meeting later on this afternoon just to kind of look at what's going on, how we're doing things, the whole thing. We we need to we need to just look at at everything and uh just make sure that we're uh the readiness is is right and making sure the preparation recovery is right. So there's a balance of both, right? You can you can overdo it and you can underdo it and you want to be right smack dab somewhere in that middle in that sweet spot. So, we're we're looking at all that stuff. >> Jaylen's obviously got a history with soft tissue injuries, but then he also was battling the ankle. Uh how much do you have to weigh the potential overcompensation of that injury or you know the fact that you do have a by-week in a week? Yeah, I I think you know there are experts who know that stuff better than I do, but I know that it all goes up the chain. And so um that's another reason why we got to make sure that um as we evaluate Jaylen, what's the best thing for him to get on the other side of this thing? Is it to see if we can get him to game day? I'm always thinking week to week. You know, I want to win this game. Um we got a huge game coming up with the Lions on Sunday night and so um I want him to be able to help us and be ready for this week. I also want to be available for the season. So we're going to take all those things into consideration. If uh Tedaro and McMillan was only targeted five times, two catches, 17 yards, >> what did the Browns do to have taken away? >> First of all, let's give uh Denzel Ward credit for doing a really good job of of following him around and covering him. Um you know, it's a tall task uh to be able to do that and to feel the confidence to. Um he did an excellent job. Team won some of his. Uh, as a staff, we got to take responsibility for putting T-Mac in great situations and um, not putting him out there where Denzel can just play him outside as much and make sure we move him around appropriately um, in as much as it fits in with the plan. So Brad and I, we can all take, you know, some accountability on that side of it. And just the targets, you know, too, it's it's, you know, some of those opportunities are man-to-man. And when it is man-to-man, there's still an opportunity for contested. Bryce can find his opportunity to get him the ball as well. So, it's all of us collectively. Um, we know we got to make team a part of what we're doing. >> Go ahead. >> Uh, building off that, Bryce, you talked about this after the game on Sunday. Um, but with Bryce having the game that he did, even without Team not really having the production that he normally does. What does that say about your quarterback? >> Battling, man. Just tough. um finding solutions and uh keeping the guys tied in, you know, really keeping them engaged on the sideline as we went through that early part of, you know, coming away with field goals, the three and outs, failing on fourth down a couple of times and just go to the next drive. Let's just solve the issues that are right in front of us. Bryce did an amazing job of that. Um and just finding ways to get Darren Waller the ball, Bryson Tmaine up the sideline throwing a touchdown to John Mechy. These are guys the tight end's room really uh coming to life for us. I was I was fired up about that. So, a lot of positives, a lot of great things that came out of it for me. Um, and at the same time, you know, there's there's a lot of areas that we still need to address to find that consistent play we're looking for. >> Apologize if this has been asked. Um, sorry, but Bryce seemed he lived off of the field. Uh, and then you kind of mentioned in the postgame presser that there might have been something going on. Was there something going on with Bryce and his and his ankle, I believe? >> Yeah, he was sore a little bit. I think he took a cleat. I can't remember exactly where. Um, so there was some there was some soreness. He battled through it, was able to finish. We're looking at him, too. You know, we're making sure that everything's right, and we don't want to um just assume that he's okay because he finished the game. So, we're going to take a look at that, but I expect Bryce to be playing this week at >> him in terms of MRI or X-ray. >> Yeah, we'll do the whole thing, you know, just to make sure. And, uh, he's so important to what we're doing. Um, let's make sure we have all the information. And uh you know, we'll I'll give you again I'll give you kind of an update on that as we get into it. >> You don't you don't know what the body part is. >> I don't want to give I it's I know that he was kicked in like a specific area and some other things. So, um I can get into more specifics later. >> These are significant injuries to significant players. Yes. >> What's the message from you to the team and then leaders of the team to try to boost morale because there were very high expectations going into this season? there's some really good football that we finished that game with um with the group of guys we're counting on for this week. And so um that's the encouraging part about it. Um talking to the guys and you know the challenge to the whole groups, coaches and players is okay, we got some stuff we're dealing with right now. Let's see how good we can be. Um and this is where the margins matter. You know, the uh the untimely penalties, um the discipline and just execution and different things. all of this stuff is really really at a crescendo comes to a head and so we all have to pull together um to continue to find really good football even if a couple of guys have to stay in there and finish the game like we did on Sunday. >> Dave, what did you guys kind of find there in the run game in the second half that you can carry through to the next week? >> Execution, uh fundamentals, pad level, footwork, um Chuba hitting it downhill and pressing the runs properly. Um it was it's all the things that matter to us that need to show up earlier. We can't sit around and wait for the run game to get going later. Uh first down efficiency. Just to say that, you know, from an offensive standpoint, whether it's the run game or whether it's the pass game, making yards, getting a new set of downs, and scoring points. We scored on five drives. That's really good. That usually gives you a chance to win the game. But if they're all field goals, it makes it a little bit more challenging. Good thing our defense down some really good play in the middle of it to keep the game close as we worked our way back into a lead. Um but then the Browns came back and executed after that. So, um we got to tie the whole thing in. >> In 24, one of the reasons why the running game works so well is the interior offensive line. Where are you at in your evaluation of them through three weeks? >> I think it's the whole group. Uh offensively speaking, um not going to just put it on the offensive line. Um it's everyone involved. It's tight ends. It's the wide receivers getting hands on safeties when the runs do get to the second level. It's our running backs being disciplined about pressing the runs the right way so that the blocks feel right so that the ball is coming to the right spot as they come off on their combos. Um handling the movement up front, different things. Um making sure that the things that we know on Tuesday, we're prepared for on Sunday. And when that doesn't happen, as a staff, we have to figure out how to help our players understand those things. And the players have to take the work in the week to make sure to expect these things, guys. So, it's not a shock to us when we get in the game on Sunday. That's how you start and play from day from snap one all the way to the end with consistency. >> Dave, is Mike Jackson is that more week to week or is that going to be longer? >> We we're still kind of evaluating that right now. So, um and he again, all these guys, they're getting imaging, they're getting opinions about different things and um and I'll have more information on that for you. How much does that impact the game plan when you're trying to game plan on a on a Monday and a Tuesday with Brad and EJ and Tracy and you've got, you know, a line out the door in the in like the MRI room. >> It's a challenge. It's a challenge because you want to know what your 48's going to look like on Sunday so that you have a specific game plan for your guys. At a minimum, we start with the opponent and we say structurally, these are the things that we do well. Here's how we want to attack. But then it gets really specific, you know, about your rush plan, about your coverage combinations on offense, certainly with the concepts that we're running. Who is catching this ball? If it's not Jaylen, you know, then who's going in there? Um, and you know, so we have to be able to look at all those things. We have to make assumptions um based on the information we have today and tomorrow to get that game plan going. But it presents its challenges. >> Two more. Two more. two years ago um when Derek got hurt kind of torpedoed your run defense. How confident are you that you guys can withstand the loss of a Pro Bowl corner like JC and kind of not have that sort of precipitous dip again. >> There's no replacing JC Horn. Um he has had such an amazing off season training camp um in season. Just the energy, the preparation, all the different things um has been amazing. Has been really beautiful. So there's no replacing that. We're not asking our guys to replace JC. We're just asking them to do their job. And um and we'll make accommodations. We'll game plan stuff and help them put put those guys in in positions that they could be successful in. Um, but it certainly takes away some of the flexibility that what we could do with JC and move him inside, follow a guy, cover Kyle Pitts, come out here and cover this wide out, you know. So, there's some flexibility challenges. Um, but again, it puts the onus on execution. It puts the onus on team football and everybody just doing their part. The guys are ready to handle that part. um just Bryce's toughness and being able to finish the game and like knowing going into this week guys are going to have to step up. Have you noticed instances where they might be looking to him on the sideline and being like, "Well, he's toughing it out. I bet I'm going to have to, too." >> I've seen that. You know, I I see guys just come over and connect and um you know, he's checking on the guys. They're not First of all, they I'm sure they're kind of more on the receiving end of it. Like he's not, you know, sitting there trying to you know, fill himself out. He's going and checking with the with the white outs, with the O line, making sure everyone's on the same page, getting back to the bench and connecting with Will and with Brad for the next series coming up. And so, um, that's the leadership that I love about what Bryce brings. >> All right. Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thanks,

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] >> 100 BPM 100 BPM >> [music] >> That's what it comes down to. Um couple of red zone and uh fringe opportunities, you know, came away with field goals, not touchdowns. Big difference there. Um missed a few turnover ops early on on the defensive side and gave them an opportunity to continue their drives. Uh some untimely penalties, some some uh some things that really hurt us and we got to be smarter in some of those areas. Got to contain the rush better. Deshaun was able to get out a couple of times, and we know the challenge of it, but we got to be disciplined with our rush and be able to do that. And uh yeah, I mean, it's those are the margins, you know, and that's what happens, you know, and you know, a lot of credit to the Cleveland Browns. The energy that Todd Monken has these guys playing with, they executed a really good plan. Um and got to give them a lot of props that way, and uh they stuck with it. They hung tight and even when we started battling back, you know, they had one more drive left in them, and um what could have ended up in an interception, but continued the drive for them after the penalty, so. >> On that play, it looked like Deshaun might have sold it. What was your view? >> I saw him get hit in the head by somebody's hands. I don't know who that was. Um but we can't do that. We have to go lower on the quarterback. When the ball's in the air, you have to make that decision right at the end to either put your hands on the quarterback or not, and um and and we made the wrong decision in that case and extended the drive, and then he was able to you know, create a little bit of extra time on the scramble play, um which is something that he can do well. And so, um we can do a better job there as well. >> Dave, you had like a handful of notable injuries, JC >> Yeah. >> Lewis and uh Coker. >> What's the update on those four guys? >> Yeah, uh JC got a quad on the touchdown play at the end. So, we're going to have to evaluate that and see where he's at, but he he was not going to be coming back in. Um Coker, his quad lit up on him a little bit, and so, um the the pain wasn't really going away. We're testing the strength, and we decided we couldn't put him back out there in that in that condition. Uh D'Onta Lewis able to come back in and finish. Um who else did you ask about? >> Jackson. Jackson. Mike Jackson. >> Yeah, Mike Jack got a groin uh kind of chasing across the field, uh hit the ground weird. Um so, we're going to have to take a look at that uh this this uh week as well. >> JC's looked pretty bad when he was not putting weight on >> Absolutely. >> Yeah, we won't know the extent of it, but I know that he was nowhere close to getting back out there during this this game. >> Why do you think the run offense took so much time to kind of get moving >> Yeah, we didn't handle the movement well front and it was it was you know, we're looking at it schematically and structurally the runs looked fine. We missed some blocks up front. We knew the challenge of this group is that they're quick. They move at the point. They do different things and we didn't handle that well early. Finally, we were able to kind of settle in at towards the end of the game and really the feature of that touchdown drive was the run game, the play actions, the offense that we know. Um The Browns did a great job covering us, making it challenging. Some of the rush patterns, you know, creating a little bit of pressure for Bryce so he had to get the ball out a little bit earlier than than he needed to. So, some things to work on, some things to look at, but I got to give a lot of credit to those guys for executing a good plan. >> After the run and all What did that do to momentum at that point? >> Well, I mean, shoot, it was just we were playing we were playing pretty well. We were covering, we were matching and the play ended up with an interception. So, it certainly was it gave us a great chance to try to be able to run the clock down. They had timeouts. You still got to execute, but all of a sudden the ball would be back in our court to be able to finish the way we want to. So, we extended the drive for them and if you give a guy like Deshaun Watson a little bit of extra time and and a few more opportunities, he's going to get creative and find something. So, that would have been a big one for us in a long drive. >> Bryce seemed to be under a lot of pressure. >> What did you see from the offensive line play and what do you think of their run? >> Yeah, there there wasn't anything too exotic. I think we might have been late one time on a slot pressure. The rest of it we had guys on guys. They rushed us well. They put pressure on Bryce and you know, Bryce had to operate that way. >> Hey, how how was Bryce was out there throwing to guys like Tremayne and Waller? >> Yeah, that's something as coaches we got to look at and make sure we're putting him in in, you know, better positions to be able to be effective for us. He certainly we want him to be a big part of our of what we're doing. They covered us pretty closely. They mixed some man and some zone. They did a good job that way. And you know, ultimately, we had one-on-one opportunities. We didn't hit a lot of them, you know, really until BT kind of hit that go ball down towards the end. So, that's just a little bit of chemistry and me to you factor, but I'm glad we have guys like John Metchie, like BT, like David Moore, who was really coming open right at the end on that last drive over the middle. I think some of they got collisioned in there a little bit, but so glad that we have these guys to be able to step in when the other guys can't go. Yeah. Yeah, he's working through something, but he was able to finish. So, I mean, we'll we'll give you guys more information on that you know, once we kind of do a full evaluation, but you know, he was cleared to go back in. He finished the game. Yeah, that's fair. Yeah, there was a couple of balls that he'll normally hit. So, I'm wondering if he was kind of working through something trying to find his base to get those balls off. He can make those throws, you know, from from different platforms and different things. He'd be the first one to tell you that up here. But, you know, he settled in. He found a way to play ball and all of a sudden we're moving the chains again and and really just proud of the way he battled us back right back into the game and the defense and the complimentary football that we were looking for showed up for us in the second half. We got to do a better job of making sure that that shows up consistently the whole time. Sure. >> the mix of the play calls, um making sure that we're balancing things and protecting tendencies. It's not horrible to create tendencies because you can take advantage of those. Um but we have a good room of guys, and we like to do different things with them in the run game, the play action game, uh different things like that. And And Darren has has his role and his package as well. Um that's something we can look at. >> It did seem like between the 20s, you guys were really trying actively to get the tight ends involved. What did you see from that group throughout this game? >> Yeah, just the ruggedness. The guys battled um and really were executing well in our boots and our play actions and the run game. I thought they did well on the edges. Um you know, it's just all of the guys playing together. We have to take that next step up front to be on the same page to make sure that our run game is efficient and effective from the beginning. That's something we have not captured yet this season. And that's something that as coaches, as players, we got to take a lot of a lot of pride in that part of it because it's it's central to what we do. >> We'll do a couple more. >> You guys went for it on fourth and one, I think, in your own 40. >> A little aggressive on fourth down, but tell me about the the mentality behind going for it there. >> Yeah, those were just right in right in our wheelhouse in terms of the decisions. Uh felt confident about those um situations, and we didn't execute. They did. And you know, one of them I thought Bryce had the corner route, we missed the throw. Um and I can't remember the first one, which which one that was, but the execution of it. We're going to do that. The guys are comfortable in those situations. We'll continue to take the ones that make sense. And our defense was playing well. And so uh we were able to kind of play off of that and take our normal ops. >> You started addressing that the Browns have been kind of going in circles to that point. They had the drive where they had it for 9 minutes, five >> penalties, punt, and then they get that short field. And then did you take that into consideration that you were potentially giving them a chance to kind of reawaken to that? >> It was a risk. Certainly something you got to think about, but um for us it was a it was an absolute no-brainer go for it. Um we can talk about the the choices of the plays and all that stuff, which we will tomorrow and you know, what could have been or all those things that of course we're going to look at those things and and try to make sure we have the right selection of things when you know, hey, if we get in this fourth down situation, what could we do on third down and and mix those things. Um but I like the decisions. >> Were you surprised they went for it? >> I was not. I was not. I thought that was an opportunity for them to try to, you know, put it away. The false start there at the end gave us life. You know, we didn't have to burn a time out, so we were able to stop them. You and and really, you know, flip the field and um and have a chance to go back down and either tie it or win. >> You mentioned how Bryce was able to get it going. >> Did it seem like they had a bit more energy than y'all did to start the game? >> You know, pregame they looked happy. Our guys were our guys were it was pretty good energy in the locker room to be honest and I love where we're at as a team. Um I love I love where we're at in terms of just the connectedness and all that, but we got to get better fundamentally and we got to make sure we execute and take advantage of opportunities in this game that we know it's a first down here, it's a turnover here and you still a you still a drive that the huge fumble on the kickoff after the re-kick was unbelievable um and really gave us a a lot of life. Um but I will say this, coach Monken had those guys ready to play building off of that momentum from last week, you know, and and they looked fired up to be out there, you know, and um we were we were able to match the energy. We did not match the execution overall. >> All right, thank you, coach. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Questions for Bryce. Bryce, you missed a lot of tackles last time. What were you dealing with or were you dealing with and why did you like to come back? >> Uh nothing is football. You know, we're all dealing with stuff. Doesn't have any bearing uh on the game. Um uh tough one. Just didn't get it done. Uh None of that stuff is had anything to do. Um just yeah, didn't get it done. >> Why do you think the running game had so many struggles >> Um you know, it takes all 11. Um you know, haven't watched the film yet. No one knows. Uh Uh I I trust our run game. We all trust it. Um you know, we you know, we're going to get it going. Um haven't watched the film to analyze yet, but uh you know, I have all the confidence in the world in those guys up front and the backs. Coaches, we're we're going to get it get it ironed out. >> I understand you haven't watched the film yet, but next gen stats had you at a pressure rate of like 52%. When you're taking that much pressure, how do you What's your process for settling in in the pocket or finding solutions? >> Um yeah, just happen to be uh just clear your eyes, all that stuff, but um again, that that's not a you know, I don't know know what next gen stats, you know, does, but um, you know, there's a lot of things that go into that, you know, it's it's getting through stuff. It's it's not just up front, you know, making sure I'm not holding on to the ball too long, getting through reads. We all play a role in that. It's it's no finger pointing. It's no specific job, you know, once I watch the film, I'll look at see what I can do better to help all that stuff out. And yeah, we'll we'll grow from there. Yeah, I trust those guys for sure. You know, we we have a lot of guys you know, stepping up. You know, there's a lot of guys that were are battling through some stuff and >> [snorts] >> you know, it's it's that that next man up. It really speaks to that room. Those guys don't um, don't flinch, you know, I trust every everyone in there. So, whoever's out there for me, I'm I'm proud of those guys stepping up. So, yeah, it was it's always good to see everyone out there. >> When you guys were able to sustain things when Cooper was out, having the game the other week, I mean, how hard is it when Nick Mullens is doing what he's doing today, two catches things aren't moving the way you guys are used to? >> Um, yeah, again, haven't watched the film yet, I have to go back. You know, first off, you know, there's there's some stuff that I can I can definitely do better. You know, obviously he's special player. He's a he's a huge part of this offense. Yeah, wasn't um, wasn't really uh, in the way that we wanted in any capacity. But again, haven't watched the film yet, we'll go back, watch it. I'll take accountability for uh, you know, us not getting it done, things not going smoothly. And then we'll we'll we'll grow from it. Appreciate it. >> You okay? >> Thank you.

text: penalties were knocking us back and that and that absolutely killed us. In the second half, we didn't we didn't have penalties. Cardinals have plenty to clean up Monday morning before a cross-country road trip to take on the New York Giants in week four.

title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 9.28.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Coach, yesterday Jeremiah was saying that the more the more carries he got, the more in a groove he got, and that was something you were talking about as well. I know it's a week-to-week thing when it comes to figuring out that distribution, but when you know that a running back is better as the more carries as they get, how does that change things around if it if it does at all? >> I I I think really it was kind of more the hot hand too, right? Like he you know, he you could feel that and uh hopefully it's like that every week, right? In terms of whoever we're giving the ball to, you can just you just know that you're going to get, you know, positive plays. Like I said yesterday, I mean it it stunk that um you know, our longest rush was only 8 yards, but but they can't they can't force that. That's those got to organically happen and and they will, they'll pop. Um lot to clean up in the run game still. >> When you went back and looked at it, what did you feel like was preventing some of those explosive both both through the air and and on the ground? >> Yeah, well, you know, on the ground it's it's sometimes um you know, just maybe a little bit like it it takes all 11. And I thought our receivers blocked really well. I thought they were getting connected, uh but sometimes maybe just, you know, not feet in the ground well enough at times. Like I mean there's there's little details across the board, but again, you don't force those long runs, they just kind of naturally pop. And then uh you know, in the pass game, I mean that's it's a real thing right now, you know, we're 3 weeks in and we haven't been extremely explosive and um I know this, when you're um you know, when you're trying to play good offensive football in this league and you're having to kind of do it through drives, drive in and drive out, I mean it's tough and I actually give our guys credit in terms of um for I'd say the good part of 10 out of the 12 quarters this year, they've done a pretty good job of staying efficient, but man, at some point we got to get a little bit more explosive. Again, you can't force that, but I do think there's been opportunities opportunities within little details uh in terms of hey, we we we got them out of there, let's check the ball down, there's a lot of space, let's get connected once we um you know, get those check down so that we can turn these 6-yard completions into 16, 20, 25, whatever it might be. So, uh a lot to clean up there, but certainly something we're searching for. >> I don't know if the teams are going maybe extra efforts to keep you guys in front of them this year. >> Um I I think that's the landscape of the league right now, you know? Um I think there's, you know, certain aspects. I mean, let's let's call it what it is. I mean, um Brock's obviously he's very good uh in the pocket, but he's very good out of the pocket, too. And sometimes when you escape out of the pocket, obviously things can break down, and so there's explosives to be had there, too. So, uh but for the most part this league is trying to limit those explosives, and uh you got to generate it sometimes through, like I just said, some of those transitions, the YAC, stuff like that. But it it's not just the player, it's it's it's all encompassing. It's everyone else getting connected on the second and third levels, right ball placement, stuff like that. So, um you know, I think uh I think we're close, but we got to go do it. >> Last week you you said that you had some opportunities over there that maybe the protection held up or whatever it was. This week where did you feel like some of those opportunities that you had kind of didn't get connected? >> Yeah, I wouldn't I wouldn't say we probably had the shots down the field uh like the the second play of the Seattle game where there was going to be something, but I I mean, we did have some opportunities to to push it. Obviously, we threw the one to uh to Michael early, but uh again, just uh you know, one little breakdown, wherever it might be, uh was kind of getting us. I mean, we were we were we were trying to call some of these play passes we need to. Um I like the where our guys were getting. I like the spots they were getting when you watch the all-22. I like the distribution we were getting. Um it's easy just to say, "Hey, that's not what we're doing well right now, so don't do that." No, that's that's the easy way out. Uh we need to be all encompassing. We need to marry the run with the pass. We need to be under center. We need to be doing that stuff. Um not just because we're hard-headed, because I do believe that's what um you know, when we get to the spot we want to on offense, that's what's going to make us as good as we can be. >> When it comes to the penalties, has there been a common denominator throughout the first three weeks that you're seeing or is it kind of a case-by-case thing? >> The common denominator is it's it's us not them. And so we got to get it cleaned up and they know that. >> Is it as simple as just getting more reps in or just going back to the tape? Like what's How do you fix that? >> Yeah, you just You got to focus in on it. You know, like I told you guys like two weeks ago, it's like sometimes you speak it into existence. I don't think we've done that. I think we've just say we know what needs to get done. We're professionals, coaches and players. We're in it with them. But but that's certainly is an aspect that has to get cleaned up because, you know, whether it was the pre-snap operation on that fourth drive or something, you know, the holding on the first and second drive. I mean, it it it killed us. You know, the third drive, obviously we got knocked back with the OPI, which I won't comment any further on that, but you know, it was there was three penalties that killed us in those first three drives and you know, against a very good team like that, it just put us in that hole. >> [snorts] >> There was so much talk, so much noise around Marvin this past week. How do you feel like he bounced back and responded to that? >> I I thought he responded nice. I thought he again he got to his spots. There were some opportunities in the intermediate again. You know, where he he's getting to his spots. So I thought he did some nice stuff and I'm looking forward to getting back to working with him on Wednesday and and continuing to grow. >> Now that you had a chance to look at the tape defensively, kind of what were your initial thoughts on that performance? >> Yeah, like I said yesterday, this is they battled. They fight. There's there's no question in my mind that we have the right, you know, it's a play style in there. But we got to do some of the little things better and it starts with coaching. We have to provide clarity and I'm talking all three phases, offense, defense, special teams because on offense, like I don't want I don't let's not mast us by 30 points. There was a lot to clean up, a lot to clean up. And it's the same on defense. And then so continue to provide the clarity to these guys so that they are in the right alignments and and doing the things necessary to play you know good team defense 11 is one. >> I I asked yesterday about the blitz rate and you said you couldn't comment too much on it but also when you guys have blitzed this year the results haven't been great if you're allowing like 15 yards per attempt or something. What do you see is going wrong when you guys are blitzing to not be able to go to affect the opposing quarterback? >> Yeah, I think I I could just use it as the same thing I just said right there. I think there's just little detail aspects in terms of blitzing blitz timing being in the right fronts all those kind of things. So again, I'm going to start with it it's the clarity that we need to provide to these guys so that they can go out and execute and execute in in a way that's you know obviously going to be successful. >> And the lack of explosives is it to Kobe checking down too quickly is it him not having time to look down field? >> a No, no, it's all encompassing. I mean it's you're calling those plays and you know I again I'll flip it to the other side. I mean a lot of their explosives were just I mean you can talk about the touchdown kid on the last one. I mean we're in sell out all out at that point, you know, like we have to stop the run but a lot of their stuff was underneath stuff that turned into it, you know, so I think they had I want to say versus Miami no versus the Rams in week one they they basically threw one shot down the field. Everything else was just a dink and dunk and guys were running. I'm not saying that's what we're going to be at. We're not the San Francisco 49ers. We're going to be who we are but uh it's it's the explosive play is is the right call at the right time with the right protection with the receivers getting from point A to point B as fast as humanly possible. Quarterback going through his progression reading with his feet and if it's not there cuz the defense dictated it check it down, you know, so I mean there's it's all encompassing. >> You can say adjustments are made every week but the first year in charge and with this scheme do you get to a point a couple weeks in where it's okay whether it's details or big picture you you think okay maybe this isn't working we need to kind of rework how we're doing things. >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I think even if we are in in their state of 10 years or 4 years with Purdy, I mean, I think um I would say any good coach uh not saying that's me by any means, but um is going to always reevaluate to see, you know, if if we're putting our guys in positions to be successful, you know, so whether that's schematically or fundamentally. Um so we're always evaluating that and again it it's I always look at it like what can our players do and what is the defense telling us that we can do or can't do, whether it be their scheme or their players, you know, so there's a lot that goes into it. Each and every week can be a little bit different, even though foundationally you're going to be, you know, somewhat the same. >> I know Zach I know Zach asked you earlier about Jeremiah and feeling like he got more in a groove as he carried it more. I'm curious, in your lifetime as a coach, have you run into a running back that doesn't say that, that doesn't say, "Hey, give me the ball more and I get more in a groove?" >> No, I mean, you want all these guys to want the ball every single time, right? Um and running back, receiver, tight ends. Um you know, our extra tackle that's playing tight end, he ran a low cross yesterday. He's a heck of an athlete. Um but um no, I mean, I no, I can't say I've ever been around a back that has said, "Take me out." Unless they obviously, you know, need one, which we we we ran a lot of offensive plays yesterday. >> On the uh flip side of the locker room, supposed to what do you feel like you did well down to down that was enabling some of that success? >> It uh you're saying >> I mean, you seemed like you had a very pretty efficient day down to down. >> I feel like I feel like we've been efficient kind of all year. Uh second half of Seattle, no. Um I've I've talked about Seattle and just our our lack of of conversion rate on third downs, but all those were manageable. Like when we are third and five or less, I feel like we're holding the pen. What I mean by that, I feel like it's advantage us. Uh yesterday we were better in that and where where weren't we better? We weren't better in in in the penalties. Um whether it be post-snap, like I said, with the with the three post-snap penalties on the first three drives that derailed it. And then the fourth drive, which we overcame a lot of them, uh but it was not near to our standard. What I was proud of the guys, if I want to flip it and be positive, is they cleaned it up. And they And um I thought uh there was good conversations at halftime amongst the players uh to say, "Hey, let's let's stop beating ourselves and let's just go play football." And again, there was a lot of things to clean up in that second half, but at least not doing those things that take no talent, um you know, gave us a chance to obviously crawl back in the game and get to a spot where it's 23 to 20 with 10 minutes to go, and I thought we had all the momentum. >> Did you feel like the the run blocking took a step forward in this game? >> Yeah, I do. I do. But But not to be confused with uh there. Uh we got a lot to clean up and um and and again, what what encourages me and what excites me about getting back to work with these guys on Wednesday when they get back in, it's it's all stuff we can control, you know. Um a lot of the a lot of the issues we had in the run game were were were simply bust. I mean, and and um our guys know that's just unacceptable. And again, anytime I see a bust, I don't point the finger at them. I point the finger right here. Like, we didn't provide the clarity obviously um to to go out and do that. >> Were there any injury Anyone come out of it with an injury that you didn't mention after the game? >> Nothing, no. Yeah, all good there. >> You were watching the film What were you seeing in this case? Watching the film and saying, "We had done this in the first half, it'd be totally different ballgame." Like, do you get frustrated with that at >> Yeah, yeah, it's all hypothetical though. I mean, it's like If if we don't do that Well, yeah, I mean, if we score every drive and they don't score, we're going to win 100 to nothing, so uh but that's not football. And uh you you know, what's the best part about this division is um the the three teams in this division, if you don't do right, uh they're going to make you pay. That's what I love about this division. And it's going to force us to to do right. >> Mike, what can you say about Jack Gibbons? It seems like he has just been in every play and just out there just kind of hustling around. >> Yeah, no, he's a he's a stud. That's a that's a great pick up by uh by Moni and and I think he fits for this defense very well. Obviously comes from a place that had a lot of success a year ago, so he knows what it looks like and he's been a great addition and I think he's just getting better. >> When you spoke with you this time last week, you said you were 4 or 5 hours into Seattle, so presumably it's the same for New York. What are the more challenging aspects of your week when they've got questions on maybe who's going to be the quarterback with the trade they just made? And maybe waiting a few days before they announce it. >> Yeah, no, I mean it it it is. I I don't know how much um how much that would change our you know, our defensive plan per se. I mean maybe situationally stuff like that. Sure, we'll go back in the you know, the history books of you know, what James has done well, what what he you know, probably wants to improve on stuff like that. So that's more situationally third down, red zone, all that kind of stuff, but so we'll we'll we'll go about it. Right now our focus is us though. I mean it's it's if we we need to clean up our ball in all three phases and I say that, you know, I I do think our special teams is has looked pretty sharp and and I've been proud of those guys, but again our standard's going to be our standard there too. Like there's another level for them to go, but we're more worried and and focused about what we're doing, not necessarily what you know, the next opponent is. >> You spent [snorts] a lot of your career out on the West Coast, so you've you've done the all the way back to East kind of games plenty of times. Is there is that a different road game for a Western team than other road games or not? >> I I haven't bought into that, you know, so I mean we're heading out there. We're playing at you know, 10:00 a.m. our time if you will. I guess that'll be what 11:00 a.m. in two couple like a month or something. Like what happens with this time change thing? I don't even know yet. Whatever it is, but yeah, no, we'll we'll wake up. We'll get our breakfast and we'll be ready to rock. >> How do you evaluate the tackling yesterday? >> Uh need to improve. You know, our guys know that. Um and uh a lot of it's is is fundamental base. Um you know, so uh but I mean that's that's just core fundamentals that that we know. And that's that's what I'm kind of getting at in terms of we got to be worried about us, you know? Like it doesn't matter who we're playing. We got to do all those things that we have more control over uh better right now.

title: TE Elijah Higgins Press Conference 9.28.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: You've heard a couple times. Yes, including from Mike McFlour that there are no moral victories, but there are things you can take from this game and move forward with it. What are some of those things in your opinion you can take from this game? >> I think those things uh include like just the camaraderie of the team, um the belief we have in each other, uh the tempo at which we play with, the belief that we can win any game, >> [snorts] >> I think and then just our play style, the way we play. I think those are uh a few of the things that he's probably referring to. >> Do you feel like >> the offense started clicking the way you wanted it to yesterday? Like after you see the film and what you produced? >> Um I have a better idea. We watch film here in like 10 minutes, so I have a better idea when when coach coach breaks it down in front of the team, but as far as just like the flow of the game, I definitely felt like we got into a much better rhythm in the second half. Um Yeah. >> Was it just the penalties do you feel like kind of slogged things up in the first half? >> I think so. >> [sighs] >> I think I mean penalties are rough. You 5 yd, 10 yd, 15, whatever it looks like. I think that was a big component of it. Like I said, uh we'll have a better idea once we once we watch the film together um and see what you know, what went wrong and you know, where we can you know, uh fix some things or whatnot, but I feel like that was uh I feel like that was definitely the issue in the first half for sure. >> When you're in the moment and that first half unfolds the way it did and then the second half unfolds the way it did, you put up a 24 points, whatever it was, and everything is just working. What's that like to be there and be like, "Okay, why is this working now? It didn't work in Obviously the penalties, but like is it is it frustrating? Is it annoying? Do you even think about it?" Or >> Um I mean, as an individual, I'm just I'm trying to do my job every play. I'm fully focused on is giving 100% effort every play and honestly, that's all that I'm thinking of to be completely honest with you. So, I think that's the best answer I can give you on that. >> Is this something you think about a win here on the sideline or like we're within a point now or even after the game you're like, if we had done this in the first half, we could have >> Um, I think there's a lot of ifs that you can ask yourself as individual. But then obviously, like when you watch the film all the plays that break down throughout the course of the game, like what if this happened, what if that didn't happen, or what if I didn't get a holding play holding penalty. It's tough to play that game, obviously, especially after you lose. But it's really just like what what can we improve improve on and you know, watching the film on Mondays always tough because especially after a loss because you've been super critical of yourself. But I think that's where the most growth happens. So, I'm excited. >> Overall, how did you feel in the run blocking game? And then what kind of attitude mindset does that take for your position to do that well? >> Individually? I feel like this year more than anything I've just attacked. Just like every play and just having full confidence in myself in my ability and my practice in my in my routine. My training as well, coach Marrone has done a phenomenal job, our tight end coach has been like stressing the importance of the details. Whether it's footwork or technique or hand placement and I feel like this is the most growth that I've had as an individual so far, not only like in my technique, but also just my mentality of attacking in the run game and trying to put people on the ground every single play. And just really finding enjoyment in that, too. I think that's the biggest thing is just going out there and when you play without thinking and you play with confidence, it's just so much more fun and so much more rewarding. So, yeah, I try I try to take that on every play and and regardless of what happened the play before, just continue to play with that aggression and that snazzy and that confidence and that conviction as well. So, yeah. >> When when Mike came in, there was kind of implied that tight ends were going to be a big part of how they wanted to do things in multiple tight ends. And obviously, that's what they did with the Rams last year. I'm curious, you've you've played in situations where you guys have had to have multiple tight ends in the past. It's not like it's brand new, but is is there a different feel to how this coaching staff uses the tight ends or how often you're using them or just what they're asking you to do? >> Yeah, I think I think this year more than any I'm as an individual I can speak for myself and my own my own role on the team, my position and whatnot. But I feel like I'm more involved in the run game than I've ever have combined in the past 3 years that I've been playing here and I think part of that is the scheme, but I think also part of that is just is my growth as a player, understanding my role and taking ownership in my role and those sorts of things, but I definitely think that there is more responsibility put upon us, um whether in 12, 11, or 13, like we're involved in the run game, point of attack, we're involved in, you know, pass pro and then obviously getting out and running routes as well. So, I think compared to the last 3 years, we have so much more responsibility as a as a unit and it's a really cool thing cuz you know, you can you can showcase everything that you're able to do and you help the team more, you know, the more you're asked to do, the the more responsibility you have to help the team out. So, I I think we take a lot of pride in that as a unit. >> You always have seemed like the kind of guy, and I mean this as a compliment, that has an edge to his game out there on the field. You you You want to talk to a a guy once in a while. I'm wondering I I you know, you're a former receiver. Not all receivers enjoy the run game, the block game, the gritty I it feels like it kind of plays into how you are as a player, that being that gritty guy, being able to like lay into a guy on a block. >> Yeah, I think uh I think for me it's just really been coming to the league and understanding like how you can create value for yourself more than anything. Um especially coming to an organization where we have, you know, if not the best tight end in the league and, you know, he's he's the guy that's run the routes and he's like, "How can I create value for myself?" and really taking ownership of that. Um and then I just helping the team in any way that I can. I talked to our unit uh a couple weeks ago and I and I said if, you know, if you're not Trey McBride, like we should be making an effort to put a guy on the ground every single every single game I kind of related to like Dennis Rodman uh of the uh the Chicago Bulls back in the day of just like he didn't score any points. Like nobody, you know, thought that he was going to score more than, you know, four points a game, but he always went out and tried to, you know, get as many rebounds as possible, uh wear guys down. Um and I think that's that's the role that I'm taking taking ownership of. Um and, you know, I'm being very critical of myself every single play uh to make sure that I'm I'm continuing to do that. >> When it comes to chunk plays or explosives, what has been missing offensively that's preventing you guys from generating those? >> To be completely honest with you, I I don't know how to answer that question. I wish I did. I wish I had a better offensive mindset and like understanding of the game, but like like I said earlier, like I just I focus on my box. I see three people and in my I'm either blocking him, him, or him and then whatever happens, like half the time I don't know who caught the ball um or who's running the ball or like any of that, so uh Yeah, it's funny like I I I don't know. I I I didn't play Madden growing up, so like I don't I don't know how to call plays. I I know the difference between cover I know the difference in coverages but like, you know, the the tendencies and whatnot. So like I to be completely honest with you, I I have no idea. Yeah. >> [laughter] >> Uh yeah, pretty much. I mean it's just midfield open midfield closed. Get the ball and just like don't get tackled. Uh yeah. I think I think it's a little bit freeing because you're not worried about too much but at the same time like I'm not going to be offensive play caller ever in my life so and I don't plan on it. So I just do what he asked me and like yeah. >> [snorts and laughter] >> You mentioned trade. How how were you improved being in the same room as him, being in the same field as him? What has he helped you? >> Um I think just the situation alone like for one seeing what it takes to be an elite tight end I think is is really flipped the switch in my mind of like okay I know what it takes, I know what I'm capable of and I know that I'm, you know, just this far away or just an opportunity away from being able to prove myself in that regard but I think more than anything it's it's taught me to to take ownership of my role that I have, excel in it and, you know, do the best that I can with the job that I have and continue to create value for myself and the team where we're fit. I think that's that's been the biggest thing for me is just learning how to prepare in a way for myself especially in the off season of like okay this is where the team needs me and being able to hone in on those on those skills and and develop those skills. That's >> You mentioned coach Morlin. Obviously he played the game as well and what ways can you see his playing experience start to translate to the coaching? >> I think I think just just the level of tenacity that he brings and like the level of aggression that he expects us like he always, you know, preaches getting into line of scrimmage and like owning the line of scrimmage and just being aggressive off the ball and getting off on the snap count and I think that that's been the biggest like coaching point for me is just attack the line of scrimmage and what happens happens as long as you have a a good fit and you're getting off on the snap, and you get in the first to contact, those sorts of things. that's been that's been the biggest thing from him, I think, for me. >> Is you had mentioned earlier that you would talk to the tight end room about like, if you're not Trey, put a guy in the ground. So, does Trey take offense to that? Are you >> Uh no, I kind of preface it preface it with the fact that like he plays 90% of the snaps, and I mean, when you're when you have that high of a snap count, it's difficult to to have that mindset. Um cuz obviously like he's running routes, and he's he's the key guy on third down half the time, probably 75% of the time, and it's like there's a little bit of a way you have to play the game to be able to show up in those situations with with the amount of like energy that you need to go run around on third down and catch a touchdown, but yeah, I think just just taking I don't know if he took I don't think he did, honestly, but >> Yeah, he I mean, there's no doubt that he can, but like I said, like I think it's just a level of understanding like what you're asked to do in your role on the team, and um and he and then him more than anybody is is is been the best at, you know, taking ownership of the role that he has and and flourishing in it. So. >> What did you see out of Jeremiah in his extended workload? Did anything maybe surprise you? >> Um I think just just just the conviction with which he runs the ball. Like every time he gets the ball in his hands, he's just he's looking for something to make something out of it, and I have a lot of respect for that. Um I never been back there in the league, so I don't know what it's like and what the vision is like and what you're seeing, but just the way he's he's protecting the ball, I think it more than anything like it has been super cool to see. and just like the level of conviction, like I said, just like making cuts and spinning every other play. Like he's just he's he's a great player, and it's cool to watch him play. Yeah. >> When I talked to you earlier in the week, it seemed to me I was didn't feel different going back being so close to Stanford, but for you and Michael and Simi to not just be on the team, but all three of you had big plays in the game. I mean, is there ever a moment where you're kind of like it's kind of crazy like all my teammates were here, but right down the road. >> Yeah, I mean it happens sometimes especially like when we're on the huddle together. It's really cool during practice and you like take a second to like look around and be like oh damn like this is this is this is like the reality of the situation we're in. But yeah, it's it's it's definitely really really cool. Um sometimes you lose sight of it, but those small moments where you realize it and you think about it for a second it's it's it's it's something to be super grateful about. >> Do you play much ping pong over there? >> Uh no, I'm not I'm no good. Yeah, they're on the table 24/7. I I I don't even think there's like space for me to get on the table, but I'm not I'm not good yet good enough to get on there yet. >> Thanks a lot. >> Thanks, man. >> Appreciate you guys. >> Thank you.

title: A cinematic recap of the Broncos' comeback win vs. the Rams | Sights & Sounds
text: And a very pleasant good evening, everybody, and we welcome you to Empower Field at Mile High, where tonight on this Sunday night matchup, it will be the Denver Broncos playing host to the Los Angeles Rams. Excited about this one. Two excellent football teams coming in tonight. The Rams picked [music] by many to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl come February, and the Broncos certainly a team that most people [music] feel like can not only be a playoff team, but a team that can make a deep run into the playoffs. And who knows, maybe all the way to the Super Bowl. Dave Logan, Rick Lewis, Susie [music] Wargin with you. Beautiful night here in Denver as the Rams and the Broncos are about set to do battle. >> there's some new stuff [music] out there. Sean Payton not calling the plays this season, right? Jaylen Waddle is now the focal point of this offense, where he lines up, the motion, all the different stuff. I think my only question is, is this defense as good as what they were a season ago? It's going to be a heck of a test for them out there tonight. >> Always one of the best visits in the league coming to Denver for a game. >> Broncos have won 14 of their last [music] 15 here at Empower Field at Mile High. And in fact, they have won nine straight games against NFC opponents. Now, to counter that, [music] the Rams have won eight consecutive games against teams from the AFC. So, something, as they say, has to give. Now, here we go with a little bit of rain as this one gets started. >> Lopsided offensively for the Rams. Two drives, 17 plays. The Broncos one, three, and out so far. >> Play fake for Stafford. They throw it in the flat, and that is going to be a Rams touchdown. Higbee with his 28th career catch. That one from 5 yards out, and the Rams strike first. >> So, Chris, give me the read on Nix. This offense off to a slow start again here tonight. >> It's going to be a conversation for a while till they get it figured out because Sean Payton's had such great offenses over the years. But I do think that Bo Nix is going to get all this figured out. >> Snap placement kick on the way and it is good from 40 on the last play of the first half. Halftime in Denver. It's all Rams. LA 16, Denver nothing. And it's just been a game that there's no other way to say it, the Rams have come in and pretty much done what they wanted to do. So, that said, we've seen this countless times over the last year and a few games. It's not over yet, certainly. But the Broncos have battled their way back in so many games. Crowd still in it, making some noise for this Broncos defense. Here's a third and seven. Dafford in the pocket, bounces around, being chased at the goal line, throws the ball incomplete. He wanted Adams and PS2 had great coverage. >> High kick, Catches circling underneath it. Has it at the 30, bobbles it but reclaimed it. Now heads to the west sideline with a good return. Like, let's this effort and what we accomplished. You can't take a step back from that. >> Y All right. Well, a lot of the docket that you see on the lefth hand side, we covered, some of which was in, you know, in bunches, some of which was in passing.
