title: Coordinator Press Conferences
text: Woo! >> Mhm. No. >> Afternoon. How's everybody doing? >> Good. >> What do you have up on the block? >> Uh you know, just some fundamentals. Obviously, it starts with me. Um I think that's the biggest thing to take away from it. Obviously, I got to do a better job um coaching the fundamentals, get the stuff corrected that we need to do, and then let the players go execute. So, I think at the end of the day, it always falls back on me and starts with me and making sure we're taking care of the fundamentals to start with, to be honest with you. >> Is that an unscouted look, you know, when they have the sixth guy on that side and then move the guy over? >> You know, uh every week we practice different things, you know, so anything that's been on film, not on film, we try to give guys different scenarios. So, I wouldn't say um it was something different, you know, but I wouldn't say it's like it's un-scouted or not been seen before in the league or anything like that. So, I think, you know, you just try to give the guys multiple situations that could occur. >> Is everybody supposed to down block on that one? >> It depends on what you're getting. So, that's why it's I know field goal protection looks like, oh, just, you know, everybody stands there gets big. It also depends on what's going on on the other side. Um, so, when you look at it, it's like, you know, is a guy moving, not moving, are they rushing straight? Um, it's obviously inside out is anything, but, you know, I guess I said it's just the fundamental techniques of like doing what we should do every single time. >> What's the challenge with their return game? >> They're really good. You know, they got a couple guys back there. Um, they do a really good job, you know, setting angles in their blocking leverage on kickoff return, punt return. They've gotten gotten vertical, you know, Tampa's, you know, they play hard. Danny does a great job, you know, all the years you look to the when you watch their film from when they're in Pittsburgh, you know, it's going to be a really good challenge cuz they're going to play physical um, with those guys. You know, they That's one thing about Danny Smith's teams is they're going to be a physical bunch and they're going to play with their hair on fire. So, we're going to have to be able to match that intensity, um, you know, from from our standpoint and do a good job, you know, whether whether it's Taggart and Teague, you know, or Kenny that's both back there on kickoff return and punt return. They got different guys that are back there that they're all quick and dynamic, you know, and they've had some good ones already to start the year. So, it's going to be a really good challenge for our coverage unit. >> Thinking about the punt return touchdown last week, is that something that affects your plan at all? >> No, I would I wouldn't think, you know, it affects your plan. I think you look at it and you see what happens and you try to diagnose it and obviously you try to replicate, you know, anytime a explosive play happens against an opponent that you're playing. Um, but I think it's more so looking at where can we put our pieces um, to generate the positive play, you know, for us in that instance the return game, you know, so, I don't think you ever want to just go say, "Hey, that worked for that team. Let's do that." You know, so I think you have to fit to what you have and the players you have and what schemes fit your guys, you know, when you watch teams across the league, you take ideas, but I don't think you just watch something and say, "Oh, that worked. I'm going to do that." It does it actually fit the pieces you have and the players and their abilities to match those types of schemes, but you start to look at any explosive play that's happening against the opponent's plan, whether it's week 1, 2, 3, what whatever week it may be. >> Did you see any I mean, concerted effort or extra effort to take Sky Moore away with Atlanta after what he had done against the Jets or did they just play their scheme? >> No, I mean, you kind of saw it if you if you really watched their their kickoff teams. I think anytime you have a guy that has explosive turn, somebody's going to try to take him away. You know, the kicker was trying to change his approach, you know, trying to dictate and kick the ball different places. So, you know, that that credit to, you know, the guys back there, whether him and Bow, they were doing a good job of, you know, changing where they were going to go. So, it's kind of like a a game of checkers or chess, you know, across the sidelines, you know, when you're going up against somebody, if they're going to change and change their approach with the kicker and and try to dictate cuz like, you know, they were jabbing and backing out and then going again. So, eventually they got to kick the ball though. So, you know, that's that's part of it, but, you know, I think as you have explosive returns and you do, you know, you look at it, it's like, "Well, who had those explosives?" You know, for us, you know, Bow had one and and Sky's had ones. We've We've got two guys both have had explosive returns. So, that that's a really, you know, good for me as a coach, to be honest with you. I feel good about both those guys back there. So, you know, they just got to decide which guy they want to kick it to in that instance. >> You put one guy back there, is that too much ground to have to cover? >> Depends on, you know, the game is so like, where's the ball going to go? Can they hit those? I mean, some people call them dirty kicks. I call them liners. Can they hit those kicks, you know? And then now you're actually covering calling it from the 19-yard line to the goal line. So, I think each week is different. I think some teams have put one guy back there and they've covered the whole field. Um I think that is a possibility for sure that you could do that. Um just kind of like I said, does it meet the scheme and is the risk worth the reward, you know? Cuz if that ball hits the ground, now that's that added hangtime and the ball's rolling and they're covering. And then if it goes in the end zone, now you're on the 20-yard line, which you never want to put your offense on the 20. So, I think you just got to maximize the risk versus reward when you do that, you know? Especially with all these kickers, I mean, they do a good job hitting these liners and these balls in different areas. So, you know, can you get to them? You know, I think majority of them, if it's a high hangtime, yeah, absolutely, you can get to them. Um it's the ones that hit the little lower balls that now you're thinking about it, is it 100% or not? >> Cam, Dan leads the league right now in punts inside the 20 through the first two weeks. Just what have you seen from him in that capacity and what you guys have been able to do in that area? >> He he's taken that step, you know, wanting to be very, very prideful in that, you know? He works that, I don't know, at practice. Um you know, and it's you're not trying to do um whether I have to take a little bit off, whether I you know, can drive the ball, um making sure we're not putting it, you know, in the end zone and then letting the gunners go play it. But it it goes back to practice with him and being, you know, every day the process with okay, which ball am I going to hit and hitting those a little bit more, maybe. Um just knowing that hey, we when we get in those situations, we got to put the ball inside the 20 um for our defense, you know? And but he's he's done a really good job adjusting that and being able to place the ball different places, too. Um cuz sometimes you you know, you want to go left, middle, or right, depending on what you're getting or what the circumstances are. >> Also asked to ask that, too. Is that a big point of emphasis for you or is that the next step for him? I think it was 18 inside the 20s versus eight touchbacks last year. And it's 9:1 this year. That's an unbelievable improvement. >> Yeah. Um, I I I think when you look at anybody as a whole, like that was an option area he could improve. And like I said, he's done a great job with it. Um, I wouldn't I don't want to say it's like a specific area for me. I think you always want to be really good in that area, right? And I think he's taken that step so far. Um, I think we still got to continue to improve. You know, you know, it's do you really want the ball to be are you going to be so aggressive and push the ball, you know, to the two-yard line, you know? Um, that that's kind of the thing, but he's done a great job. Like we sit down when we when I got here and and him and we talked about areas needing improvement. That was one we worked on and and we talked about. So, it's it's so far it's been the results we want. Um, we just got to continue to do those and continue to work on it. You can never stop working on something just cuz it looks good right now. You got to continue to work on it, you know? And that's the fundamentals, whether that's kicking, blocking, whatever it may be, running. You got to do those every day. Um, so you maintain, you know, and you can improve and you're never going back. >> With the injuries that have happened just on the offensive line, how's that affected you from a prep standpoint during the week in terms of who's available, who might be out there and where? >> Uh, rotate them all, you know? Kind of like any position. We talked about like lining guys up there the other week, I guess, several deep. It it's kind of, you know, when you're when you're talking about offensive line, you're obviously mainly talking about field goal protection. Um, not necessarily. [snorts] I mean, you could put them on different units, which we've got guys that potentially could do other units, too. But, um, it's just a rotation and maximizing what each guy can do. And like one guy may be a guard, but he also may be a tackle in the end, so he's got to rotate. And you've got to funnel those guys in cuz you never know when a guy's going to go down and who may have to sub in and who may have to fill in and and you through a game. And that's I think every situation and that's every position. Um and you just got to be try to be strategic and play the mental gymnastics about if this guy goes down, who am I moving? Um and that's the biggest thing is for us to do the mental gymnastics and rotate the guys. And it may be a walk-through. You know, not everybody can get reps. But in the meeting times and stuff, it may just be like, "Hey, get down here, get some footwork." Or after practice, you know, come give me five field goal steps and protection stuff. Just little things that if you have to put a guy in a different spot, he's ready to go and it's not like you're putting a guy in there that's never done something. Um for me, that's that's a big thing I try to prevent is having to go play a guy that's actually never done the technique at a position. >> Anything else? >> All right, great. Y'all have a great day. Thank y'all. >> Thank you. >> Good. What do we got? >> What have you seen on tape so far from Daniels? >> Yeah, going through it right now. Um obviously kind of a little bit of an unknown, you know, but he played in preseason, looked at some college tape, but they got a really good offense, man. They got good skill guys. Their O line's good. I think Zach Robinson does a really good job um pre- and post-snap with how he affects your rules. We got to be on the details. >> Also to ask, do you watch a bunch of college tape? >> Yeah, we try to We try to turn over every stone. >> What did you see from the run defense the other night? >> Not good enough. you know, I think uh just basic fundamentals of playing football and how that relates to um playing the run better. We didn't do at a high enough level. So, it starts with me. Um we got to do a better job coaching up our guys, you know, that hasn't been an issue, and it was definitely an issue Thursday night. So, we better get that cleaned up or it's going to keep showing up. >> How do you assess kind of where you're at against the run when you've had two strong performances and then Atlanta >> Yeah, I don't think it's like go back to the drawing board. I think we just got to uh coach and play better. I know that's cliche, but it's the truth, you know, obviously give a lot of credit to Atlanta and what they did. Um you know, I thought Bijan had a really good night. He missed He made us miss some tackles. We had a lot of um I would call them cup violations. We got to do a better job caging the ball. Uh when the ball circles you, it's typically not good, you know, and we had the ball circles us circle us a couple times. So, but we got the same challenge coming up, you know, with between uh Bucky Irving and and Gainwell. with Gainwell in Philly for a little bit. I mean, if if you give them the your edge, you they're going to take your edge. So, uh we got to do a good job set edges and build the wall and tackle. >> Coming out of the Jets game, did you see any sign that, you know, your run defense would collapse like that? Because it looked like you played the run pretty well against the Jets. >> Yeah, I think for for 2 weeks we've played pretty good. I I mean, you know, it's Thursday night football and you don't get to practice. Those aren't excuses. We got to play better. We didn't play well. You know what I mean? So, um like I said, just get back to the technique and fundamentals of what it takes to play good run defense. Um you know, and obviously you know, sometimes runs pop, you know, by what you're in, you can have a couple hard downs, but you got to get the ball down for 10. They can't go for those huge explosives like we had in that game, and that's where the yards and the points get out of hand when you're giving up explosive plays, so in the run and pass game, truthfully. So, I wasn't pleased with we were at where we were at. Um way too many explosives in that game, and that's not a recipe to win games, you know, or do our part to help us win games on defense. >> Mention the numbers, obviously, almost 500 yards, 35 points. Were there any positives, any bright spots that you took away, things you liked? >> Long time ago for me. Not a not a ton, honestly. No, there wasn't. >> What can you do from a pass rush perspective when teams get the ball out that quick against you? >> Uh you got to tighten the coverage, you know what I mean? So, if if teams are going to get the ball out of quarterback's hands, and you see that all throughout the league, it's a it's a blend of you know, tightening up. Um then when you tighten up, you know you're going to they're going to try to throw the ball over your head, you know? So, it's kind of that give and take of different coverage structures, matching up with the rush, rushing cover, um and just doing a good job of mixing it. >> Joe, what happened on uh Hooper touchdown? I think you had a timeout right before that, right, to to discuss it? Was that >> We we uh communication standpoint, the in the the third and goal on the five, >> Yeah. >> we weren't in the right call. Falls on me. >> What do you think happened after the the roughing call that extended the drive? >> Well, we gave up an explosive after it and then we didn't hold up in the red zone, so it led to points. So, um continue to coach our guys about, you know, how we got to play penalty free, you know, through you know, education and and technique and decision making. So, um that hurt cuz we were off the grass there. Um but we'll be better. >> When you go up against a athletic quarterback like you're going to face this week, is it like in essence probably a combination of everything, but do you have to rush carefully? but the job that you have to do if you're too careful, do you just go attack? Cuz how do you How do you Without giving away the game plan, how do you handle a guy like >> Yeah, I think you know, cuz you see um a lot of mobile quarterbacks now, it seems like, doesn't it? You know, um where it used to not be like that. Now, it's like every week there's a mobile guy. But um you you know, if you're you got to do a good job of rushing together, is how I would say. Whatever the call is or whatever kind of call you're in or structure you're in, um you got to do a good job of rushing together, meaning that if if a guy's counting on something else happening and taking the appropriate rush, that other things that he's counting on happening needs to happen. Um so, we just got to do a good job of detailing how we're going to rush this guy cuz he's definitely mobile. Like you saw that. Um and when he gets out, he he can generate explosives. So, no different than playing Kyler or Carson or um you know, I guess Michael to an extent, but um this guy definitely that's going to be a challenge of defending the pass um versus this guy is is rushing him the correct way. >> What do you think about what you've gotten out of Wyatt [clears throat] through three games? >> Yeah, I think he's in a good spot, you know, he's playing a a of plays. Um I think he's still catching his groove, you know, but he's doing some good things and I think he'll keep impacting the game. >> Do you have a feel for what your strength is as a defense? Do you know that after three games? >> I wouldn't say that. I I think our play style has been on point. I will say that. Um, I always think we can generate more takeaways, but we've shown that we can capitalize on some ops. Um, you know, like I said, it's hard after that game where you say the run defense is pretty good. I think we have the appropriate amount of uh, rushing cover, covering rush staples that are in. And then it's up to me kind of make sure that we're keep putting our guys in proper positions to affect the game, but I think some guys are playing pretty good ball right now. Collectively, we all got to be a little bit better. >> Dennis Sutton played a lot the other night more than Thrash. Um, what have you seen from Dennis Sutton here getting him more and more opportunities? >> Yeah, I think he's doing a good job, you know, I mean, he's like like, you know, like anybody, like they're competing for playing time. Um, that's kind of the nature of the NFL and that's maybe how the game went a little bit. Um, you know, what goes overlooked with Baron, he's playing a lot of snaps on teams on fourth down. Um, but I think they're all our edge guys are doing a pretty good job of defending the run. When we drop them, they're doing a pretty good job in coverage and got to continue to find ways to affect the passer. >> You had you watched a lot of film of your players this off season and your off season programs, training camp. With this being your first year though, is there still learning going on >> Absolutely. Every day is a learning experience to me. Um, you know, [snorts] and and that's a that was kind of been a not a cool thing, but for Thursday night football, you get a little bit of a a weekend to kind of just watch your play for myself. Um, kind of watch, you know, what spots we're putting our guys in and where they're having success and where they I to improve. Um, and start you know, really owning in on that a little bit, too, you know, and and that's my job to make sure that I'm putting them in good spots where they can impact the game. But, um, you know, they had they had a good attitude on Monday. I'm sure they'll be ready to go when we come back in here tomorrow. Okay, thank you guys. >> [clears throat] >> Do you think 10 years later you'd still be coaching Laken Tomlinson? >> Yeah, I I was laughing about that when he showed up. The first time I met Laken was kind of in the circumstance like this when I was with the 49ers. And we traded for him right as the season was starting to get to get things rolling. So, yeah, it's it's crazy how things work in the league. Um, but I was glad to see him. >> What do you think he still has left to offer? >> Well, obviously he's a vet. He's got a lot of experience. Um, you know, he's been through a lot of this before as far as just different defenses, different calls, things like that. He's familiar with this offense um, in a lot of aspects uh, with the familiar familiarity with he had when with San Francisco and the New York Jets uh, when he was when he was there. So, I think he'll acclimate pretty quickly. Um, we'll obviously see how it goes at practice and everything like that, um, to see where he's at. >> And how close guys start if you Is it possible they at least >> Yeah, I think anything's a possibility for sure. So, we're we're going to do whatever we can to put the best guys out there. We got to see where they're at and um, you know, just where they're at with the playbook and the calls and everything like that with the game plan. But, yeah, everything's a possibility, and we're going to try and you know, explore all avenues. >> I know it's not unusual to get guys in during the course of the season, but I'm not sure how many times that you've had it two starter level starter level quality guys come in in the middle of the season. What's the process of getting them up to speed? So, >> Yeah, I mean, the process basically, you know, you find things that they're familiar with, and you know, this is like this, this is like that. Um and then, they look at whatever you give them, the game plan, anything like that that they have questions on, then you kind of go through all the different scenarios that can come up um situationally. We big with calls and third down, you know, the third down menu and everything like that. So, um yeah, it's just a process, but again, when when you have guys who are veterans that have played, um you know, there's a lot of familiarity with a lot of different things when you when you've been around a few places. So, I I anticipate mentally they'll be able come in and help us um as soon as as soon as possible. >> Is it Is it best to play them at the spots they've been the best at? >> [clears throat and cough] >> Like Lincoln's been on the left side a lot, right? >> Yeah, I mean, yes, it's always best to do that, um but we got to look at what's best for our team, too. So, it'll be a combination of both of that. >> I don't want to take a shot at Jager or or Moncrief. So, it's not to plant the question, but it's got to give you some peace of mind that you have to go from two really young guys who are kind of learning on the fly to guys who've been there, done >> Yeah, that's the tough part, you know, when you have a bunch of young guys in there, um in those big moments, um that's always hard. But, those guys competed, and you know, again, they were not crowning anyone the starter or anything like that. So, we're just going to take the week as it goes, um and just kind of evaluate it from there. >> Steno, how do you make sure Jordan doesn't fall into bad habits because he's sped up so much back there? >> Yeah, I mean, it starts obviously with the pass protection. Everything starts up front. So, the biggest thing is just making sure we do a better job. We got to do a better job covering guys up. We got to do a better job sustaining our blocks. So, that's that'll be the biggest thing we obviously need to keep focusing on. >> In general, what do you think you do well right now offensively? >> Not a whole lot. Um you know, we have an explosive offense. We really do. But, we just got to make sure we run our offense. And that was the thing we didn't do that Thursday. You know, we we've had a lot of hard conversations. Some really productive conversations. I'll just leave it at that. But, we just need to run our offense. >> With the running backs, obviously, what happens up front kind of dictates how things unfold for them. But, for that position specifically, are they getting the yards that are there? Are they finding ways to create more than once they're at 10? >> Uh yeah, I mean, we just need to we need to try more in the I should say invest more in the run game as the game goes. I think that's one of the biggest thing that's going to help the quarterback. It's going to help the O line. It's going to help everyone if we if we really try and run the ball. >> I don't know. Were the guys up front sticking to their rules? And and maybe Atlanta was doing something different than what you were expecting? Or were they >> Not really. There was one There was one pressure where they got through and hit Jordan pretty hard. And that's something we have to fix and make sure that doesn't happen. That was a good pressure by them. But, other than that, it was just guys not sustaining their blocks and things like that. So, we need to do a better job. >> So, not like a ton of assignment errors, more physical than >> No. Yeah. Not a whole bunch of that. >> So, how do you better handle those stunts then in [clears throat] of that they're running? >> Yeah, we got to do a better job covering guys up. I think we're being The one thing I talked to you know, with the offensive line about is just making sure we're more proactive in our sets. We're more aggressive using our hands better covering guys up. I think you know, these guys some of the younger guys are playing a little passively. So we got to make sure we're playing more on the line of scrimmage and being more physical in the pass game. >> So pardon the dumb first question like but when the end loops around to the inside I don't know if this is a game plan question or that you can share but what's the how you supposed to handle that? >> Yeah, we got to snap that twist off. The guard's got to use his hands and snap it off. The tackle's got to take over the penetrator. It's a pretty basic twist so we just got to make sure we do a better job picking that stuff up. >> At this point in the season do you usually have a feel for your strength or or what you're going to do well later? Is it odd [clears throat] to be >> It is very odd right now. Yes. I I think I know what our strength is right now. But you know, we still have a lot of new pieces here if you think about like our tight end room. Pretty much all those guys are new or half the guys are new. We'll see you know, what happens with the offensive line this week. And then the running backs a lot of guys haven't played a lot. Chris Brooks has but other than that so we just need to keep playing ball. We need to trust the system. We need to trust each other. We need to trust our technique and we'll come out of this. >> Was Lloyd an instinctive runner coming out and what do you how do those instincts seem to you right now? >> [snorts] >> Well, he hasn't really gotten a chance to get going in my opinion. None of the running backs have so I'll hold off on that question once we get him a few more carries. >> You said at the start of the season it's going to be running back by committee for a while. Would it help to maybe lessen the committee and stick with the guy to get him into a rhythm, maybe? >> Yeah, we've talked about that. >> I mean explosive side of it, but the start that Christian's been off to so far, what have you seen from him in that regard? Just kind of how he's sort of stepped up in there. >> Yeah, he's been huge for our offense. You know, anytime anytime we need a big play, he had made a huge play on a third and long uh where we really needed something happen um and he did a nice job there. And he's just kind of a guy that we've been be able to rely on uh to come through in those big moments. Um obviously down in the red zone, he's doing a nice job scoring touchdowns. So, uh yeah, he's he's come through big so far. >> A lot of those lines with Christian since he came back from that injury last season, it feels like he's just been >> super productive. What Is there something that's different about returning or >> I think, you know, probably when you go through something like that, you you kind of have a different perspective and a different hunger, you know what I mean? When you have to sit and watch and and not play and watch your guys go out there and compete. So, I mean, that's a question you're going to have to ask him, but he's always been pretty dialed in. He's always been uh pretty motivated kid, so um you know, I I think just as he gets more experience playing, he just keeps getting better and better. >> He sounds pretty critical of himself with the drops the other night. I think he was targeted eight times or something like that. So, obviously you tried to get him involved, but >> just how important is it for the offense to really get him going? >> Yeah, I mean, he's definitely one of our best players. So, anytime your your really good players don't play well, it's going to be hard to be good as an offense, you know what I mean? So, I think he's obviously as critical as anyone about how he played, and I don't expect that to happen again. >> What's the challenge that you guys face against Stanford's defense? >> Yeah, they're um really good against the run. Really physical front. They play with a lot of guys in the box. Their safeties are very active. Um they challenge you in a lot of man coverage situations, so we got to do a a nice job of getting open versus man coverage. Um third down they're going to pressure. Uh people are going to keep pressured us till we show that we can uh stop it. So, we got to make sure we do a really good job handling that. Um and yeah, they're just a a good physical defense. >> Good. All right, thanks guys. See you. >> thanks guys.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Mhm. >> Mhm. >> [music] >> Woo! >> How'd you spend these three days? >> Doing stuff. >> Uh spent some time in the office and then let the guys get out for the weekend and kind of everybody get a reset and ready to go. >> When you say reset, is that enough time to make significant changes to what you're doing on offense or do you have to just kind of fine-tune it at this point in the year? >> Um well, I think it's you know, this league it's week to week and you're always fine-tuning. Um certainly we've got to we've got to go out there and and execute at a higher level. So, I think the bulk of the emphasis moving forward is we've got to be better fundamentally and that goes across the board. >> Will Mical practice this week? >> He will not. >> How can Tomlinson and uh Becton help you right away? >> Potentially. I mean, we haven't been out on the field with them yet, so it's it's tough to say, but I think as we progress through the week, we'll we'll have a better indication of that. >> What's realistic when when you've had these guys that you've gone through the off-season with, you've gone through camp with, and now you may go a different direction. Like, how Just how do you go about this? You've never really faced anything quite like this before, right? >> Yeah, I mean, all you can control is how you respond to every situation, and you know, we're going to attack it head-on and try to get put the guys out there that we feel give us the best opportunity to go win a football game. >> I know it's They have to get acclimated, they have to learn a playbook, and all these other things, but what does it do for you to get two veteran guys who potentially could be big contributors for you? >> Yeah, I think it's it's great. I mean, these guys have played a lot of football, so, you know, they know how to play the game, and you know, the game's not too big for them, but it's certainly there's there's going to be a learning curve there. >> What is it like trying to get them up to speed and help them navigate that learning curve as quick as possible? >> Yeah, it's just meet. And you have a lot of meeting time, and then, you know, when we get our opportunity to get out on the field with them, you got to maximize that time. >> Tomlinson's basically played only at left guard for the last several years. Would it Is that ideal to keep him on that side, or can he play at right guard as well? >> I think he's got the versatility to to go either left guard or right guard. >> Which spot do you feel is best for Becton? He played both tackle and left guard, obviously. >> Probably uh more so on the right side. That's primarily where he's played. >> Either at guard or tackle? >> Yes. >> Banks going to be available for Sunday? >> Uh again, another guy that we got to work through the week, and we'll see. >> Is Micah still on track? It Have there been any setbacks in his recovery? >> No setbacks, just part of the process. He's got to get cleared before we can let him get get out there. >> You've obviously faced both those guys before. Um what are your recollections of of playing against them? >> Yeah, just really good. Obviously big big people. Um you know, that that have played a lot of ball that can come in and potentially help us. >> When it comes to the offensive line player, are there aspects where you can kind of go back to square one and build up from there? Is that too difficult to do in the season? >> No, I mean the fundamentally it's we've got to get better and I think that's where uh the majority of our focus will lie is in terms of our pass sets and and um how we're passing off twists, how we punch, all that stuff. It's got to improve in a hurry. >> You talked about passing off twists. What Why has that been such a struggle for this offensive line this season? >> Well, I think if um if we if we did a better job, we wouldn't be talking about it. So, it's just it's one of those deals that both guys got to be on the same page and you got to you got to stop the initial movement. You got to flatten those guys out in order to pass them off. >> Is that a vision thing during the play? Is it recognition before the snap, communication either way? >> Uh all it's all of the above. I mean, you got to be sometimes there's not tells for when it's coming, but I think situationally you know, like if you're in known pass situations, you've got to expect that some of that stuff can happen. >> I understand fundamentals are important, but like did you there's no way you envisioned that your offensive line struggling to the degree that it has in the first three weeks. Has that taken you by surprise and are you are you second-guessing anything that you guys could have done differently to prevent where you're at now? >> Well, I think it just goes to show if you get into a game where you feel like you have to drop back like that. I mean, it's it's tough in this league and I think you're seeing D-lines. I mean, a lot of these D-lines are pretty darn good. So, um I would say first and foremost, you got to stay out of those situations as best you can. Obviously, there's going to be known past situations, um 2-minute, obviously long you know, third down can be that. Um but it's just tough when you're in the third quarter and and you start to resort to that. >> You you've proven over the years that you like to run the football. I think the first 15 plays on Thursday night, I think it was 12 passes and three runs. Now, that's not Some of those are cans, right? It's just you calling them. But do you Are you thinking, "Okay, I need to go back not to necessarily Tennessee with Derrick Henry, but are you thinking you need to just figure out a way to run the ball more?" >> Yeah, absolutely. I think it just keeps defenses at bay, a little bit off balance, um and then you're just not getting hard chargers at your quarterback in every snap. >> What kind of predicament are you in though as a play caller? Cuz you know that you need that balance. You know that you need to call more runs, but you're not getting the efficiency there in the run game, and you just kind of feel like you're running into a a brick wall when when that happens. So, like, how do you balance that out between knowing that you need that balance, but also it's not working for you? >> Yeah, I I I think that's that's always the tough question. I mean, you got to Sometimes you got to stick with it, and sometimes in early in games it may not be working to the level that you would like to in terms of the run efficiency, but I think they're like body blows in a boxing match. You just got to keep throwing them, and and there's a lot of things that that play off the run game. So, we got to do a better job. I got to do a better job with that. >> Any more clarity on how long Jaylen Reed might miss? Is he He going to have to go to IR? >> No, I I don't have any updates on him. >> What did you and J.G.'s >> Sorry. >> Excuse me? >> You mentioned after the game Thursday night you feel you got the right guys in the locker room to get through this. What was your message to them after their weekend off when you got them back together? >> Well, I just think you I I first asked them how many guys watched games throughout the course of the week and I think 12 of the 14 games were one-score games. So, the these games are battles. Um and it doesn't matter who you're playing, when you're playing, you got to show up and be your best each and every Sunday. So, um it's it's just more or less you got to keep fighting. And sometimes in some of the games that we saw the scores were lopsided early and teams just kept fighting and battling and were able to overcome that. So, I think that's the main message and then ultimately, I I you know the one thing that you love about this league is just the the attention that it gets. I mean, there's a lot of interest in the National Football League and um that's that's a blessing, but you got to drown out the outside noise and we got to focus internally and at the end of the day, all that really matters is what our guys believe in the locker room and how we're working together and and trying to find solutions for our problems. >> Uh what did you see when you and JG looked at the run defense and and what happened? >> Yeah, what No, he's an elite player. I mean, he he's one of the best in the league at any position. Um I I think that there's some things we can do schematically and then there's some things that we absolutely have to execute better. I mean, we had what we call cup violations where you know, the ball breaks contain and you know, they're they're getting more yards than what should be there. So, bottom line is it takes everybody. It takes the call, it takes and then it takes everybody doing their job and doing it at a high level. >> It seemed you guys had You've some work on Campbell in advance of Sunday with Biggers going down. What does that do just to challenge you guys as far as a completely different style of quarterback? >> Yeah. You know, we're we're kind of diving into that right now. Um certainly you you never expect that. It happened on the last, I want to say or one of the last offensive plays for them. So, there's an adjustment there and our guys will work through that, but Daniel's has shown we've seen a little bit of him in the preseason and he's a guy that through the scouting process coming out in the draft, very talented player. Certainly can beat you with his legs as well. He's got a big arm. So, um there'll be a little bit of an adjustment there for sure. >> With the running backs in the run game, what have you seen from that group in terms of getting what's available or being able to generate more than maybe what's blocked up? >> Yeah, I think that's one of the things, whether you're a running back, quarterback, D-lineman, you got to get allow guys to get into a rhythm. And I don't think in certainly if you run the ball nine times, it's hard for them to do that. So, yeah, are there are there opportunities to get more there in some instances? Yes. And then um you know, sometimes not every run has to be an explosive gain. You just sometimes you just got to go hit it and get 3 yards and it's 3 yards in a cloud of dust just to kind of stay on schedule and and set yourself up for some more manageable third downs. >> You're saying after the game that he needs to process quicker, but if you look at what he's done through three games, I think he's got the quickest time to throw in the league. Is it possible for him to actually process quicker and still run the offense that you want to run? >> Um I would say there are certain situations, yes, but then there's a lot of times where you know, the the rush has been hitting home quick. So, again, it it you got to look at what you're asking your guys to do and what we're doing schematically and you know, we've got to do a better job of of mixing it up, I would say, so it's not just all these longer developing plays. Certainly we we love explosives. Um he loves them, I love them. Uh they typically lead to points, but we just got to be a little bit more timely, I would say, when we're when we're calling them. >> Coach, I I I know there's a lot of fires you're putting out, but did you feel better about um reducing the number of penalties on Thursday night? And then what do you think of what Watson's been able to give you? He's been an awfully bright bright spot. >> Yeah, I thought I thought that was Christian's best game. Um you know, he was fighting for extra yards, he was making plays down the field. Uh as far as the penalties, yeah, that I guess if there is a bright spot, there was it was less. It was still too many. Um and there were some unnecessary ones. Um but you know, there's there's plenty of to still clean up and really in all three phases. >> Thank you, guys. >> All right. Take care.

title: Jared Verse & Deshaun Watson Press Conference | September 29th, 2026
text: The way he's the defense has improved from the first week to where you guys are now. >> Yeah, I think it was just us becoming who we are. You know, I think that first week was a bad character, bad show of character and you know, I think we needed that to really knock us in the mouth. And now I think we are we're not where we want to be yet. You know, we're still giving up too many points these last two weeks, but we're getting there every week. >> When you talk about how you know, you made your goal just to run through your blocker's face So, you had always kind of mindset going into Why did you make that switch in mindset? >> I think I I think I listened to too much of other people. Everybody talking about oh, you need this move, you need that move and I forgot what got me to the point I'm at, which was genuinely just running through your face. Like if you're not stronger than me, I don't care how you know, these guys are 320, 330, it doesn't matter. I'll still run through you. Like you got you're going backwards while I'm going forwards at full speed. Like I'm just going to run through you. So, I forgot you know, that's my superpower. So, I said let me make that you know, big statement, a big testament this weekend. From there on, work everything else off that, but it was working too good to switch from it. So, I just kept doing it all game. >> Jarran, what do you think of the start that Mason's off to? Four sacks in three games and just having that type of pressure in the middle of the defensive line, how beneficial is it? >> Oh my god, it's amazing. I mean, you know, he's getting back there so quick, the quarterback's starting to run around, you know, whether he even gets the sack or doesn't, he's getting so much pressure and everything like that. It's making it everybody else's job easier cuz they you know, the tackle has to hold on to him a little bit longer. It gives us the chance to take the edge and you know, I think it's a it's flourishing every week. It's getting better and better and I it's just joy to play next to him. Like he's a it's a ogre. >> The old days, the old days, those inside guys used to be like big fat dudes. How have you seen that position evolve and those guys become more dynamic in their role in the defense over time? >> I mean, in my what is this, year three? In my years playing in the league at least, I haven't been with any fat guys. I've been with elite, fast, you know, interior tackles. So, it's just it's just it's like a different version of you on the inside. Like they're super fast, they're super shifty and they get back there quick, but you know, you you got to turn that edge quick too cuz it's a race to the quarterback every time. >> Could you have started training camp thinking you could get off to a start like this? >> I'm not surprised by it all. I knew who who Mason was before I even got here. You know, before even the trade happened and everything like that. I knew who Mason was. I knew he was going to be hooping. And to see how much work he puts in, I mean, you see it all the little highlights on Instagram and everything like that. But when you hear every day and you see what he's doing, it's not surprising at all. >> Did it look like Bryce was feeling you guys sometimes on Sunday even when you weren't there yet? How how How much do you guys feel that and notice that during the game? >> Oh yeah, you can tell, you know, quarterbacks start getting a little nervous back there, a little antsy. You know, cuz nobody wants to get hit, you know, and you when you're thinking about anything else but making the perfect throw, you're going to like a couple bad throws, you're going to get a little antsy and start running around. And he was making some bad throws because you know, Mason's getting back there. Malik's getting back there. Isaiah's getting back there. I'm getting back there. BB, like everybody was just getting back there you know, certain points of time to make him frustrated and constrict that pocket. >> Steelers made a couple O-line changes before last week. Did you see it show up against the Bengals? >> 100% I mean, I think the right side, you know, Yeah, their right side has definitely lifted up a lot more. I think they're really athletic. I think they've gotten a lot better at handling pressures, handling, you know, these games and these rushes that they've been going up against. But you know, I think we've gotten better, too. So I think it's going to be exciting. >> It seemed like both you and Quincy Williams decided in the same week to stop trying to be maybe something other than what you've always been. And you both kind of got back to being your sort of aggressive, intense self. Do you see what I'm saying? Do you sort of see it that way? >> Yeah, 100% I mean, I think me and him had the similar mindset that since we came here we had to be the superhero, the Superman and everything like that. And that's not who I am. I'm not like that, you know what I mean? The Hulk don't wear a cape. I just run through people. I'm just aggressive. I think Quincy's the exact same way. He's just aggressive. We all just got to do our one of 11 instead of trying to do everyone else's job. >> You're good. >> I'm good. >> Thank you. >> Thanks, sir. >> Sorry, excuse me. >> I'm trying to get you to talk about the excitement of going into this game, Thursday night football, Steelers coming to town, the way the crowd was on Sunday. Just what are the emotions heading into this one? >> Uh it's huge. It's major. It's a great opportunity to showcase what we're about um on a on a you know, big national stage. And um yeah, we're super excited. You know, we just you know, ultimately, you know, as a locker room, we just stay locked in. Make sure we got our craft and everything that you know, our game plan is uh so we can go out there and execute at a high level. You know, we we're playing a very uh tough opponent, experienced opponent. And um we got to make sure that we have all our all our things locked in going into that game. >> Deshaun, when you um jogged off the field at the end of the game last Sunday, um kind of met by AB at the locker room. You guys kind of had an embrace. He had some words for you. I was kind of curious what what his message what was to you after that game. And um just kind of how do you describe your relationship with AB? I know Coach T even said, you know, he's glad that AB is your QB. But how would you describe that relationship over the past couple years? >> Yeah, um you know, me and AB always been right there. He's always communicated with me throughout the whole process. Whatever was going on, what we're doing in the QB room, what we're doing uh coaching-wise, you know, everything. So, he's always communicated. We got a great relationship. You know, and then we just continue to build from that. You know, we built that trust and that honesty where we can just talk to each other. And um you know, we just hope that we can continue to build that and uh win a lot of games together. >> How do you feel personally about showcasing your comeback in prime time games to the rest of the NFL? >> Yeah my my main focus is the game playing clean football having opportunity for us to be able to win the game. You know that's all I'm locked in on. You know I'm not you know getting too caught up in all the antics and in the media and things like that. You know I got to make sure I lock in. You know this is a very humbling league. You got to make sure that you locked in one game at a time. You can't get you know keep the main thing the main thing and that's playing football. >> What are your impressions what are your impressions of the Steelers defense? >> Very real good defense. Like I mentioned very experienced. You know the up front guys they've been there for years very active. The secondary got a lot of experience guys that played a lot of football so they do a lot of different things and you know you know they they create a lot of turnovers so you know you got to make sure that you you know seeing what they're doing and and getting the ball in the right spot. >> You've been in the AFC North for a little bit you know these games are a little grimy or does that does the defensive nature of some of these games is that make you adjust maybe how aggressive you might be does ball security become even more of an emphasis potentially? >> I wouldn't say if it's if it's more you know cuz every game that's number one priority you know the ball ball security is the hopes and dreams of the whole organization the team and the city you know so you got to make sure you take care of that. So going and thinking about ball security is always been number one what priority into every game but yeah these games get you know definitely intense and you know these are divisional games and you know rivalry games and you know it's a little bit more energy for sure. >> What about being in the concussion protocol now and then you might have to work with another starting center what impact might that have on the game? >> You know same mentality as man up. Luke has played a lot of ball. I've been with Luke for the last three years so I know what he's about. We communicated, we worked together before, so yeah, we we super excited for the opportunity and praying for for Jenkins to get healthy, so he can get back in this locker room with us and we can have him around. >> We've seen a lot of penalties on the offensive line in the first 3 weeks. Mostly you know, with the formations, the false starts, things like that. What type of role do you play as far as helping correct that, minimize that, so that your job doesn't become harder than it has to be with negative yardage getting tackled on? >> Uh that's a big role, you know, that's where the communication come in. What am I doing to, you know, what what can I do to make their jobs easier so we don't create those, you know, false starts. Um you know, the illegal formations, making sure that everyone is aligned correctly, making sure guys are hearing me, hearing the play call in the huddle and communicating a little bit extra in the huddle so the guys know which way to go, so um again, we have a young team, new offense, a lot of moving parts, but you know, [snorts] at the same time as a as a as a quarterback, you know, you got to take a little bit more charge and to continue to do that and make sure we cancel out all those things. >> year, how do you Deshaun, how do you get your how do you get the vertical passing game going a little more, you know, is it being taken away or what can you do to get a little more explosives in the passing game? >> Yeah, I mean at the end of the day you got to take what the defense give you. You know, I think teams know we want to be explosive, but at the same time, you know, you got to let it come to it. You got to have but actually once you try to force those explosives to throw it down field and now you're sitting in third and long, you know, and those are wasted plays, so um you know, you got to take when those opportunities come and and hit them, but at the same time you just if it takes 20 plays to get a touchdown, then hey, that's what that's what we going to do. >> Deshaun, how about that? How much can some of those those runs that started to to break out in that game on Sunday, Quinshon's 11-yard rush, uh the 17-yard uh run, how much can that help create explosives down the field if you can get that run game going? >> Yeah, it can definitely help cuz now the safeties and secondaries trying to cheat up and now you get your one-on-one matchups outside and and downfield. But, uh, yeah, we got to continue to try to be balanced as possible, uh, create some good running run uh, run game and run it rushing yards so we can, you know, get the secondary kind of, you know, biting up and we can try to go over the top. But, you know, it's all part of the different game plans and different schemes that every team is trying to do to us. >> Do you have a relationship with Aaron and what's it like to see him playing like he is at the age he's at? >> Uh, not like a real true relationship. I've known Aaron just passing throughout the years playing against each other. Uh, when I was working with Dr. ElAttrache on my, uh, shoulder, he was out there with his Achilles. So, I got to talk to him a little bit. But, man, it's it's it's, uh, motivating. It's inspiring to be able to see what he's doing at the age that he's doing it for so long. You know, I was watching him as a as a young kid and just being able to now, you know, play against him is is super dope to see him on the other side and you can learn a lot from him. Um, and, you know, it's just it's cool to see one of your the guys that you watched and looked up to for a very long time, you know, on the other side. >> Between him and Brees, Brady, Peyton Manning, why do you think quarterbacks are playing a little longer these days? >> Um, I have no idea, honestly. I'm not even sure. So, I'm not even sure. >> a lot of You made a lot of plays with your legs so far, especially Sunday. >> Do you think you're any quicker or slower than the surgeries before or you still got the same speed and quickness as before the surgery? >> I'm not sure. I'm just reacting. I'm just playing ball, man. So, if I look fast, I guess. But, if not, I don't I'm not sure. I'm just playing ball. So, I'm not even thinking about it. >> Deshaun, how about your connection with K.C.? It didn't go the way you wanted it to on Sunday. So, what can you guys do to kind of get that thing going for you? >> Yeah, I mean, it's just again, you know, there's different looks. So, at the same time, these guys are rookies. Kasey and Boston, especially playing any receiver or any person that knows that playing in the slot in the NFL is is a lot. It's a lot of different moving parts, a lot of different coverages. They can match, they can zone off. You got linebackers, defenders. So, you know, it's it takes some time to be able to recognize and see all the different coverages and things that defenses can do. And it's week to week. Every team is different. You're not going to get the same that you did in Tampa versus Carolina. And same same thing moving forward on Thursday night. So, uh that's just kind of the more reps, the more experiences that we get playing with each other and seeing the same thing, you know, it'll get better for sure. >> two more. >> Knowing that the support that you got from the fan base Sunday, are you kind of itching to get back in that stadium in prime time on Thursday night against the rivals? >> Of course. Yeah, I mean, the energy, the the excitement, the positivity, everything. We fed off that. And I feel like that was a big part of that win um on Sunday. And we want to continue to feed off that, especially against this opponent Thursday night prime time. And, you know, we want to showcase that, you know, we're going to play really good football, put up a lot of points, make some excitement, get the cheers going, and defense play well, play all three phases really good, so we can get a W. >> We saw you talking to coaching up Kasey after after one of those incompletions where Carolina almost picked it. I wonder what was your What was your point of emphasis there for him in the first half? >> Yeah, it was just a return route. So, again, it's just what I what I mentioned with Mary Kay. It's just the different looks. You know, you might feel like he's zoning off, but, you know, with your return route, you don't necessarily pick. You just keep coming underneath it. So, that's what I was selling him. It's just, you know, that's reps again, being on the same page. I'm expecting him to return underneath underneath that DB and kind of catch it and run, but he kind of sat, and I threw it inside, and the guy made a good play. So, you know, it's learn, you watch the tape, you correct it, and you know, and the next time we'll we'll be on the same page. >> It was more of a And then, Rod, can you see yourself still still playing in 12 years? >> That's the goal, man. God willing, for sure. God willing. That's the goal. So, you know, I want to play as long as I possibly can until football tell me I can't. Thank y'all. >> Mhm.

title: LIVE: Brian Schottenheimer Press Conference | 9-29-26 | Dallas Cowboys 2026
text: Bye-bye. Heat. Heat. Heat. Go cowboy. Heat up here. up here. Go cowboys. Heat up Go Cowboys. I heard I heard >> um in that case Joe >> uh Joe Hoy, Dallas War News. Obviously you guys are into a action afteraction reports. Um, how did that process go with that with the last 28 seconds from that game and what's your biggest takeaway in reviewing that? >> Well, I didn't do very good in the last 28 seconds. Um, I think when you talk about, you know, finishing the game, you know, which I really think you look at our two games that we've lost, you know, Joe, we haven't finished and I was a big part of this one. Um, like I said, I talked about, you know, after the game, you know, I felt like I over coached Dak on third down. Kind of affected his decision-making a little bit and I let that kind of bleed over to my decision about kicking the ball. Uh, my dad had a rule uh, one play at a time. He talked a lot about cuz it happened to him. He made a decision uh, on a play. It didn't go good. He was pissed off about it and it affected another decision. And I think that's kind of what happened to me. So, uh, I'll take accountability for it. Uh, it's football and life. It's what happens. Uh, but I heard our chance to win that game and, uh, uh, I'll be better and, uh, I'm better than that. I'm better than I performed in the last 28 seconds. >> And in terms of the over coaching with Dak, um, what lessons do you learn from that? What kind of conversations do you have with him about that? >> Yeah, he and I talked on the plane. You know, again, I'm not going to get into too much of it because there's some schematical stuff. Um but there was a lot going on and um you know some of the words that I told him have meaning and uh it put him into a uh mindset where he just kind of checked CP and then felt a little push and threw it away. So um again, you know, we've got built in and I talked to him after the game and as a competitor he should be pissed, you know. Uh but uh again uh he and I are great. >> Brian Todd Archer with ESPN. Can you kind of walk us through the how the game management stuff works? how many different voices you have talking to you and ultimately how these decisions get made. >> Yeah. Well, I'll take you through the whole sequence actually, Todd. You know, I mean, so we get the PI penalty down there to CD and uh it's first and goal from the two, we call a run and uh we have a we have run tags for our elite players on the outside if they're one-on-one that we can do different things. And um they played one-on-one so we took the shot to CP. Uh second down, felt really good about the call. Uh unfortunately we had a false start penalty so that kind of moved us back. Uh so we had to adjust at that point. Uh second down I thought Baltimore did a really good job. They they covered the concept that we had. So Dak did a nice job moving up and scrambling. Uh we called timeout immediately because you know you wanted to make sure you have enough time to to score. I mean we were not trying to tie that game. You know we wanted to try to take uh the victory and and take the lead. Um Terrence Steals on the ground you know. So then Brick goes in and then third downs where I over coach Dak and I put him into a a mindset he normally doesn't play with. So that's that's where I made the mistake. And then like I said at the end of the day, you know, when you when that happens, you know, you have to move on. At that point, I'm no longer the the play caller. I'm now the head coach. And the communication with Nick and feeder wasn't good enough. And so that starts with me. And so um take responsibility, take accountability for it. But uh again those uh those things will not happen again. >> And then the defensively was there any a decision that should have been different? >> No, I think the coverage was okay. Uh we played way too tight and there was an error on that play where we should have made the ball go to the low hole player, the low underneath guy, not the deep one. Um but I think you know CP and I have talked and um there were some other calls he he would have liked. So that's that's my point. Like again, as a leader of this football team, I take complete responsibility for the last 28 seconds. It's on me. I own it. I will be better because of it. But as a football team, in the our two losses, we just have not. We've made too many mistakes in the fourth quarter. I've always said games come down to what? The fourth quarter. You can't win the game in the first, can't win the second, third, fourth. You win it in the fourth quarter. And that's where we haven't been haven't been good enough as a football team. And then Jerry was on the radio today saying there's no explanation that you'd be satisfied with. What were those discussions like with him? I'm sure you you probably weren't satisfied with your whatever you had to explain or whatever either. >> Oh, I mean I'm I'm man enough to take mistakes, Todd. I mean, I make a lot of mistakes.
