Uh how is Patrick feeling today after that hit? It looked like he was kind of wincing and grabbing for his back a little bit yesterday. >> Yeah, I think it it was you know, more than a chiropractor could do. So, I think every bone in his body cracked on that one, but he uh he got back up and kept firing. >> And then the the the first play he talked to us about it post-game that it maybe wasn't intended to be that roll-out. The one where Travis was wide open for 48 yards. Can you just give me a glimpse of how that that unfolded? >> Yeah, they end up pinching inside on it on the right side. So he just moved a little bit to the right and threw back to the left there. Yeah. >> All right. >> Thank you, coach. That's all we have. >> Okay.

title: Kansas City Chiefs vs Miami Dolphins - Official Postgame Show | Chiefs Rewind
text: The Chiefs are 3 and 0. Everybody on Mitchell. >> Under pressure. >> UNDER PRESSURE, SACKED AT THE 31-YARD LINE. THIRD DOWN, THROWS A WHEEL UP RIGHT SIDE. IT'S CAUGHT! TOUCHDOWN AT THE FAR FRONT PYLON. HERBERT IS absolutely eaten alive. It's Drew Tranquill. And the pass is going to be Oh my goodness, WHAT A CATCH by Tyquan Thornton. And here comes a rush, and he's GOING TO GO DOWN. GEORGE KARLAFTIS. >> [music] >> The Chiefs are 3 and 0. Hi, everybody. I'm Mitch Holthus, voice of the Chiefs, along with Matt McMullen, senior team reporter and director of editorial content. I get that right? Yeah. Uh but a 24-10 victory. Now, if you take the first two possessions and two of the last three, you get 24 points. It was in the middle where the Chiefs had zero. >> Yeah, you know, it wasn't always pretty here today, but they all count the same. We will take it. And we were joking around about this and maybe a couple years ago, I'm not sure how people would feel about a win like this. But after last year starting 0 and 2, I will get the 3 and 0 however we can. I'll take it. >> Yeah, and 3 and 0 is 3 and 0. And we anticipated Miami in a home opener and a young team that's feisty would give a fight. And they did give a fight. They just stayed alive and the Chiefs couldn't put them away till those last two of the last three possessions. >> Yeah, I think the Dolphins players and coaching staff deserve a lot of credit for how they played in this game. And we talked about it. The danger in a game like this is allowing the opponent to hang around because they start to believe. I mean, these young players for the Dolphins, they have nothing to lose. And they don't know what they don't know. So as the game went on and it was close, they were really into it and playing good inspired football. Credit to the Chiefs though, being in a hostile environment like that where it was hot, it was humid, the opponent has nothing to lose and wants everything, uh, nothing more than to beat you. Uh, the Chiefs found a way to win this game. And that's all that matters in the end. >> Thought it was going to be easy, right? A four-play 67-yard drive to start it including Kelce for 48 yards. And then to get a touchdown on the next possession. But give Miami credit. We talked about their defense. They had some interesting schemes. They were not going to let Kel Walker get out the gate and run for 200 yards. >> Yeah, and in the big scheme of things looking at the schedule in the year, maybe this is a good thing for the Chiefs that we had to win in a different way. So the first two weeks Kel Walker is just running wild and the opponent has to load the box and they can't stop him still. Well, today, I mean, he still has a decent game. He goes for 18 carries, 70 yards, had the two touchdowns and a 22-yard, uh, run which was a big play. But I mean, we didn't couldn't rely on that all game long. Had to win this game, uh, on Patrick Mahomes' arm and he found a way. >> Yeah, last year the 18 for 70 would have been like the best performance of the >> [laughter] >> year. No kidding. The grading scale here. And then defensively though to get three fourth-down stops. Now, the Dolphins give Malik Willis credit and their offensive line, no sacks for the Chiefs. But to get three fourth-down stops, we'll talk about it even more here. But those were gigantic plays. >> Yeah, so the defense, there's some areas for improvement obviously after this game. Uh, Uh need to clean up the big plays and the third downs. Miami was eight of 16 on third down in this game, but yeah, the stops. So, L.J. Sneed with a forced fumble and recovery at our own 31, huge play. Monster DeLaine with one of those fourth down stops, a pass breakup on a slant. And then Noah Williams, the pass breakup on the fourth down late. Some big plays there for the Chiefs defense. >> Let's get reaction now from here in Miami at the podium. >> Really, we didn't have uh so far any injuries to report. Um Listen, uh we My hat goes off to the Dolphins and the job in which they did. Jeff did a nice job with that with that group. They're a young group like we are and they they fly around. We knew it'd be four quarters of football and uh that's what it took, so um uh but we got we got plenty of things to work on, but it's great to be three and 0. And uh uh there were some real good things we could take out of it and there's some things we can definitely work on um going forward, but I I thought the second half uh we we had some stops defensively. I thought we did a nice job there uh with that and then uh took advantage of a couple of those with uh uh with the offensive side. So, um and then special teams were were solid. Anyways, we're out of time, gentlemen. >> [clears throat] >> Andy, what do you like about their group now? You know, only two games, there wasn't a whole lot of film to see and different personnel groups, a lot of young guys, but what what did you think and I guess what sort of match your assessment of film coming in about where half of this kind of fits >> Yeah, the the one thing I mentioned to him was these guys play hard and they play hard every snap. And um and that's a that's part of That means they're listening and trusting him and uh that's a that's a positive that he can he can build on and he'll do that. He's a sharp guy, so uh he'll you know, he's got a good staff, but they they play hard. >> All right. Okay. Thank you. >> Okay. >> We were talking about having warm fuzzies here with the Super Bowl 54 win, but you had a bunch of folks here. You grew up watching the Dolphins here? >> Yeah, I definitely grew up watching the Dolphins and um the Miami Hurricanes too as well. >> Okay, let's talk about this game, how you got the early catches and kind of got it going. Talk to us about those early plays. >> Um I think one of the catches was on third down. Um they played a lot of zone coverage, so I just kind of found the soft spot and Pat delivered a good ball and I just had to come down with it. >> And how much has that been a work in progress for you going all the way back to OTAs of working against zone and being on the same page with Pat? >> Man, definitely. I mean in zone, I mean route depth and just being on time that's very important. So I feel like versus zone me and Pat have a good you know, kind of a sense of timing and where he need me to be, so um we'll be on point. >> I said this uh I people got fired up last week with your two long ones and you had a long one in this one, but I'm as fired up about your middle routes. You and I talked about it, how much you worked on it. What about being a middle route receiver as well as a deep ball threat? >> Um it's definitely important. Um the ball come out a little bit quicker, so you definitely got to have your eyes ready cuz they're coming through traffic. You got the big guys and the linemen and stuff too, but um definitely decided to you know, expand my route tree and go out there and make different catches just not the deep ball. >> You and Tyquan Thornton is with us. Uh then things kind of got bogged down. It looked like hey, two touchdowns, two drives, going to be 50-point burger, but then what happened because the Dolphins kind of made things tough. >> Um I feel like it was really just us, you know, um just making little slight mental mistakes, you know, but um not playing clean football. But I mean we kind of got back to it, you know, trying to play some clean football. O-line got going and we was able to finish the right way. >> You guys have done such an outstanding job of blocking uh whether it's a run or those screens. What about that as a point of emphasis for you as a wide receiver core? >> Um it's definitely important going out there blocking. Um I was just blocking on the DB and Kenneth Walker busted outside, you know, so just just knowing that you have a back like that is kind of encouraging knowing that he can make those type of plays and cuts. >> How much money did you spend on tickets for this game? >> Too much money. Too much money. >> It's worth that number two and the Chiefs get the victory here 24 to 10. Tyquan Thornton. >> Yeah, I mean, at the end of the day, we won the football game and and we found a way to to to to win and and win by two touchdowns and um obviously we didn't play to our standard that we would we would hold for ourselves. Uh especially in that middle part offensively of the game, kind of second quarter through third quarter. Um but I thought we we felt we found a way to come together at the end of the game. We had two great drives at the beginning of the great game and now it's about learning in the in between and so um it'll be a learning experience for us to know that we have to come with our A game every single time in order to win. Um but at the end of the day we're three and out. >> To that to that point, it does really reinforce the week-to-week nature of it. Is that something you can impress on your team and talk more like So, dynamic >> 100%. I mean I mean we're young. We're a young football team and so guys have to learn that and there there will be learning experiences throughout the season. Luckily luckily enough for us we still won won the football game. Um but I mean these guys like you have to just continue to press that this is a long season. Like just cuz we had a first two weeks good weeks against good really good opponents doesn't mean that you can you can relax when you're playing a 12 o'clock game, you know, and so um a lot of these guys first 12 o'clock game, first time traveling um and having that experience in the NFL. Um and so for them um learn how to get themselves ready to go faster so that we can go out there and play better football. Yeah, for sure. I mean and then that's that's just going to part of it is I have to continue to work the pocket and find places to throw. I thought even the ball to Rashee, I slid it in the pocket and then I tried to to a throw and I left it behind them and ended up getting bounced up for an interception. And so, um that's about me finding my feel for the pocket again um in some of those critical situations. Um but uh we just got to get better as an offense. I mean, we we scored 24 points and we did all those things, but at the end of the day we left a lot out there and uh we're not going to be mad about getting mad about winning. We won the football game and I mean, you think about last season we were losing some of these games. And so, um we're not going to be mad about winning, but we're going to look at the tape hard, find ways to get better uh for next week. >> Play action just changing the game for you? Cuz it seems like that's when you find your rhythm, your success in these first few games. >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, it it's it's helped me out a ton. I mean, it's I think people look at the stats and they see like the touchdowns that Kenneth has and that Emitt when they're running the ball and and the run game that we're doing, but I don't think they really understand how the play action and the movements and stuff like that has really opened up in our offense. And that's a credit to them, that's a credit to the offensive line firing off the ball, run and pass. Um and uh something we have to continue to get better at marrying as the year goes on, but I I thought we did a great job with that today. Um being better in the dropback passing game. Um like I said with the ball to Rasheed was a was an open throw I could make. Um and some of some other little things here and there. Um but other than that, I thought we did a we did a great job. It's just about finishing drives and not making those little mistakes. No, he got me. He got me for sure pretty good. Um but that's part of playing football. It's they they they brought a good stunt with the D-line and um I tried to get the ball in my hand. When you throw the ball, you're kind of exposed and um he got he got me pretty pretty solid. But uh like I was able to bounce back up there and we went out there and finished that drive. Yeah, I think we're just guys are just going out there and finishing. You know, I think that's training camp. We had such a great training camp. It was like it wasn't always pretty. Like we have like I said, we have a lot of young guys and we're all building chemistry together and it wasn't always the prettiest, but guys pushed through and pushed through. And I think that built that up um for games like this and um we didn't it wasn't always pretty on both sides of the ball. I mean there was times where um we were kind of getting we were that three and out after we get in the flag coming out of half and I thought it just defensively they they stood up whatever they needed to, made big plays, stopped them on fourth down. Um but like I said, we got a lot of stuff to clean up, but uh I was proud of how our guys finished the game. >> Patrick, you're three and oh all time at Hard Rock Stadium. Just you you won your first Super Bowl here. Can you talk about the nostalgia of coming back and and winning today? >> Yeah, no. I mean I think just that when you get on the field you kind of feel that. I mean you're just looking around and seeing the stadium where you won your first Super Bowl and even at the same hotel room. So like just being going to get to the hotel and I'm like I'm texting some of the guys that were around cuz we had a full it's been a full week here and it was like guys would come to your room and you'd and you kind of have that team bonding uh stuff going on. And so um it it was cool to kind of be back here and and to play this game. Um at the end of the day you got to go out there and play and so it was good to get a win. >> Okay, the defensive sequence at the end of the sequence of the game you got hit and then the touchdown pass was incomplete. I just wondered like what was kind of your emotions in those >> Yeah, I think it was just kind of letting out the emotion of like this hasn't been the way that we wanted to be and um it was that frustration coming out in that sense, but um we were able to make the play, you know? Like that's at the end of the day the most important thing um letting out some of that frustration there, but uh uh Travis making a play. I mean he caught the first pass and the last pass. I mean it was uh it was uh him battling through that as well and just making the play when his number's called. >> Does it feel like you've got more ways to beat teams right now than you mentioned in the play action things you did today or just some drop back stuff that was working? >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean first of all I mean just the run game in general run the ball so well that defenses have to change how they play against us and um we're going to continue to do that. Um it's continue to run the ball and then play action off of that, keep defenses honest um movements and then have the drop back. That's what you want in a great offense and a great team is being able to beat you in many different ways. And and today we showed that with the defense making big timely stops and then us scoring when we needed to score. Yeah, I wouldn't say I feel disappointed. Like I'm happy for the win. I think last year kind of taught me that you can't you can't be disappointed when you when you win football games. You have to enjoy every single one of them. Enjoy the plane ride back, everything like that. Um but I know we can be better. I know we can get better and that's going to take watching the tape and going out and having a better week of practice. Communicating within the entire offense and the entire team. >> We're going to be happy. We're going to enjoy this this victory. But we know and if we want to get to where we want to go we have to continue to get better and better. And so we'll do that. It's probably the favorite thing I do in general is with the the Gladiator logo and sponsoring these teams. Like high school football was so important to me and I still am best friends with some of the guys that were my receivers and my running backs and stuff like that in high school. And so obviously it's cool what I do with Texas Tech. I love that. Everything like that. But giving back to the youth like you said, letting them get that logo on their their jerseys. I remember how important that was for me. You'd wear it to school on the Fridays and then get to go out there and play. And so there's some great high schools down here. And I'm excited for them to have that logo on their jersey and going out there and represent the right way. Yeah, no. The I mean the first one I think the fact that I scrambled out to the right kind of got him open which it wasn't necessarily supposed to happen like that. I was supposed to pull up but the how the defense line stunted I was able to get outside. And I think what got him open the most is Ta'Quan running down the field. I mean you have that speed running at you down the field. The safety got got depth. The run game, the play action brought the the first level, second level up and then all of a sudden Travis is right there behind everybody and so got him the football there and he made a big play and then the last play was just part of the read. You could tell they were they had some confusion. We got out of the huddle kind of quickly and snapped the ball. They were trying to figure out where to go to and so Noah had the the out route. I kind of gave him the eyes to him. Kenneth was underneath kind of holding that level and so then I just put it up and when you have a big tight end like that he can make a big play and go up and get it and so big play big time play for a big time player and helped win us the game. >> Just to clarify, same hotel room specifically? >> Same same hotel room, same room number, everything. So it was it was cool, you know, like I didn't even feel the nostalgia until I got there and you see the room and I'm taking pictures and I'm I'm sending I remember last time we were there we were watching like some type of like show on TV and we and all the guys were in in my room and that team bonding you'll never you'll never forget that and so it was it was cool to kind of send it to those guys and tell them that I'm back there and I try to win. I did not ask for I don't ask for any of the rooms so I just got to I just kind of kind of happened that way. >> Yeah, appreciate it. >> Go for Chris. >> Chris, guys probably want some things back but it's a really happy locker room describe the meaning of winning like that where it's not all perfect. >> Yeah, we're going to have those games where we face a lot of adversity. I think coming in today we didn't start how we wanted to but we was able to get the win. That's the beauty of it and we know this game isn't easy to come by. >> How proud are you of the way the team responded after the first half and that stuff? >> You know, that's just who we are. I mean we knew they was going to come out punching to a young team who is building explosive quarterback, running back. Mixed it up on us in the run game, blocked it up, threw it down field a couple times so I think we beat ourself on a lot of it. We got to figure out you know, where we messed up on and correct those areas this week and um we move forward. Won the Super Bowl, yeah. Can I be honest with you? I don't even remember. Listen, it was staying at the Turnberry. Felt so good. I like everything was amazing and um just very fortunate we got the win. >> I think it's more so don't let a a good play or bad play affect the next play. It's all about the next play and um you know, um the first Well, the first quarter was very up and down on our end as a defense and kind of pull us together and let us know don't let the good play or the bad play affect the next play. He's very explosive and the tempo plays is where our offense uh you look at the first three um third downs. One of them was a screen. The second one was a quarterback draw and the third one was a screen. So, kind of gets you off your game when you mess it up like that and then you make a move when he's going under. So, I think he kind of um schemed us up on that, but we still got to get to the quarterback. Find a way to get to him. >> [panting] >> I I think that's just the NFL. Um no matter the record of a team, um we all are professional. We all come to play and we all got an opportunity in in front of us. No matter what your record or what teams you beat, uh it's a new challenge every week. So, um I think they'll take from it that nothing comes easy in this league. Thank you. >> Chiefs get the victory here 24 to 10 over the Dolphins. Chiefs are 3 and 0. No sacks. Dolphins had given up nine in the first two games, but I saw something I was really encouraged about. I want to get your thoughts. Passes deflected. Chris Jones got a deflection led to a Karlaftis interception. We saw Christian Ronald Wallace maybe not touch the ball, but affecting the aerodynamics of the throw by Willis then then it got knocked down, but the ability to affect a pass at the line of scrimmage. And that did not really happen the first two weeks. >> Yeah, we talked about that in training camp that some of the best Chiefs defenses in recent memory were great at knocking down passes at the line of scrimmage. So, in 2022 and 2023, we led the NFL in batted passes. Those defenses were obviously pretty good. Not so good last year. Well, that was an emphasis in training camp. To your point, didn't really see it in the first two weeks, especially last week. I mean, Daniel Jones was zipping the ball out of there. Just had to get our hands up. Maybe that game goes a little bit differently, but here in this game, guys are getting their hands up. That's a big deal. >> If you've got a real fantasy league, then keep track of batted down passes or passes defense at the line of scrimmage or anything >> for that. >> Come on. I mean, that's huge plays and the fourth down stops. Uh two of the three uh were that. Uh but also to see Montre Diggs-Lane on the field. He made the slant uh deflection on uh fourth down. But what he means now to this defense and his presence not just against the pass, but aggressive against the run. >> Yeah, he had a great tackle for a 5-yard loss early in this game as well. You can see it with Montre Diggs-Lane. He's obviously going to be a star and uh hadn't seen him a whole lot this year. Didn't play a lot in training camp, obviously dealing with a shoulder injury. Uh played well in that first game against the Broncos. The first couple of snaps had the interception, but then got hurt and didn't play last week. It was awesome to see him get out there, play a full game, and make some plays. >> 61 times Mahomes has gone to Kelce for touchdowns. That was a big time play on that corner route. >> Yeah, it was. Awesome throw there by Mahomes. He was fired up after that. And interesting game for him. He finishes 20 of 24 for 246 yards and two touchdowns. It was kind of funny on that last touchdown to Kelce. It was like, all right, enough with all these shenanigans. Like we're going to get out of here with a win. Enough of this. That's why Patrick Mahomes is is the best to ever do it. So, uh another good game for him and you know, most importantly, we got out of here healthy. I mean, it was hot, it was humid, it was miserable out there. And again, the Dolphins were playing with nothing to lose. For us to win this game and get out of here healthy, that's a win in its own right. >> Pat took some shots in this game though. >> The chop block. Yeah, he is tough. A little high-low he wasn't happy about. A final thing about Patrick, 115 wins now. That counts playoffs and regular season. He ties Tom Brady now for the most wins, regular season and playoffs, of any quarterback in their first 150 games. >> Wow. >> What a milestone. >> Yeah, really incredible. We can't normalize all these numbers with Patrick. I feel like every single Chiefs Rewind we're talking about some record that he's set. One other thing that stands out to me though, if you go back to last year, the Chiefs had lost six consecutive road games. Winning on the road is hard. Now, there was a lot of red in the stands here today. Kind of felt like a home game at times, but still, winning on the road is hard. We began last year losing on the road. To go and win our first road game of the season, I think it's pretty important. >> That's a really, really good point. Now, the Chiefs are 3 and 0. Now, it's 3, 2, 1, Raiders week. >> there. >> And it's going to be a big game in Vegas on Sunday. He's Matt McMullen and I'm Mitch Holthus. Chiefs get the victory here in Miami, this glorious place where we were celebrating after Super Bowl 54. Chiefs Rewind is brought to you by Ford, the official car and truck of the Kansas City Chiefs, and by Community America Credit Union, the official banking partner of the Kansas City Chiefs.

title: To special teams coordinator Brian Mason, the Spencer Shrader of last September is back
text: Obviously, I'm sure everybody's going to want to talk about Shrader a little bit. Really good game from Shrader. Um, obviously, he made his PAT, went four for four on field goal, made the game-winning kick. There wasn't anything out of the ordinary uh, you know, with him during the week. There wasn't anything out of the ordinator starting warm-ups. Obviously, there's always load management and things that you're trying to work with with kickers and trying to be aware of those things. Um, especially, you know, he and his past has kind of overkun some things. So, we're always kind of cognizant and aware of that with him. I thought he looked really good in warm-ups. And we're speaking like honestly here like I watched him in his first set of warm-ups and was like, "Holy cow, the Spencer Shrader of last September is back. Like this guy looks really good." Um I thought last year in warm-ups, he looked as good as any kicker I've seen live. Like he was really in a spot where he was on fire and things last year before his injury. I thought like, hey, he's really getting back in a rhythm right here and looked really good. And of course, right after I had that positive thought, he ended up stopped kicking. So he said, you know, he had some tightness or some pain um that he felt. Uh you know, whenever a kicker says that, you never know what the there's varying degrees of I have tightness in my quad or my groin or my adductor. You don't know exactly what that means. Only the kicker is going to know the level of that. We shut him down at that time. We took him to the training room, had him get evaluated, had him get worked on. He had full strength, so that was a positive sign that, hey, this isn't something serious. We have a luxury that we have two guys that are really good at kickoffs, right? All right. So, hey, right away, hey, he's going to be able to kick in the game. We got to get him back out there. Um, once we they worked on him in the training room to, you know, see how all that looks, we got him back out there. He was kicking on the sticks. The biggest thing was, hey, just don't be thinking about this thing is that might not be easy to do, but you just got to stay within your process. Um, not, you know, obviously, um, be thinking about, hey, something might be off. You got to stick to your normal process. I think he ended up settling back into doing that because we have Rigo who's really good at kickoffs and has experience doing kickoffs. We just took that off of Spencer's plate for the game so that he could just focus on field goal and not have to worry about extra ball contacts and exposure. Usually a kicker does like doing kickoffs because that allows them, especially in a game maybe they're not getting a lot of kicks, that allows them to continue doing ball contacts and stay within rhythm of the game. Just didn't make sense for him to do that within this game. Thought Rigo did a great job um you know being able to do kickoffs for us. Uh you know, a luxury that we can have both those guys. That's something that we'll evaluate as we move forward. We can still use both those guys based on how kind of things play out during the week um and how things get evaluated with the training room. We expect Spencer to be able to go no problem. We'll we'll limit or load some of his management based on what the training room tells us throughout the week. But obviously, we saw him kick during the game. He had five kicks in the game. Three of them went over the net. He did an unbelievable job staying locked in and staying in his process. Had a great game. Expect him to be able to move forward this week in the exact same way. and we can limit him as needed based on what the training room tells us. But he did a really good job. Bit of a roller coaster, but an awesome job. Rio did a great job. Kickoff team did a solid job. We won the kickoff drive start um by eight yards. I thought the kickoff team has been really solid at We had one really bad rep to start the season where one guy didn't do his job. We've been locked in. I thought they've been solid ever since. We had another opportunity where we got a ball to hit into the landing zone and roll into the end zone for a touchback to the 20, which was great. Obviously the end of the game we trust our our kickoff unit to be able to do their job. Um so we were able to burn 5 seconds at the end of the game make a tackle at the 30 31 yardd line which is the expectation. We did that twice last year. I think it's huge if end of half or end of game you can trust on your kickoff unit to be able to do their job to burn time. Like hey we can trust on you guys to tackle the ball in front of the 35 yardd line instead of just kicking a touchback and conceding the 35 yardd line with all time. We can trust on you guys to do your job and burn the time because at the end of half of the game, the most important commodity is time. We did that last year in the Falcons game going into overtime. We did that last year in the Seahawks game which was not the end result we exactly wanted. He got the ball to the 35 yd line, but we did burn six seconds and them doing that. We want those tackle to be around the 30 yardd line like we did in this game. Pump return-wise, uh we had a really nice 20-yard return. We also had another one where we let hit the ground, which we can't let happen. Unfortunately, he lost the ball in the sun, but you know, obviously we practice every single day outside. That's a situation that we should be better at. Um, and can't can't allow to, you know, obviously them flip the field ping out of their end zone. We only had one kickoff return opportunity. I thought they did a great job blocking it to the kick side. There's a little bit more there. We got it to the 37. Would have liked to seen even more. We got kind of tackled by an arm tackle up around the 37 yardd line. A little bit more opportunity to get going there. Punt team only had one rep. Did a nice job with the 47 yard net. We'll do just a few questions. Joel, go ahead. >> What uh what challenges does the roof present for you guys when it's open versus when it's closed? >> Um you know, I think obviously, you know, if you ask the specialists or some people, they certainly would prefer the roof to be closed. That is obviously, you know, provides different, you know, situations uh for a variety of different people depending on the conditions of the day, right? It did seem to be a very bright and sunny day. Um, which was, you know, by the angle of the way things were at was right in the eyes of guys as they were looking to catch balls or catch punts and things. And I think there could be some common sense that is used as we interpret some of this stuff. That's not what it said in the rule book, but that's the way they officiated the play. So the way that they interpreted it was not exactly the letter of the law in the rule. Hey, as a coach, just tell me what the interpretation is and what word the rules we're playing by. So, that happened in that game. They're interpreting the rule to be that way. I don't think that that's the intent of what the rule necessarily is um or what everybody would like for that rule to read. So, hey, a holder was really supposed to be used on kickoff when there was an issue with weather. Traditionally, in kickoff, they kick off from the 35, the kickoff team, entire unit is at the 35 yardd line. So, if the ball blows off the tee, you would take one of the guys that was already lined up at the 35 yardd line to hold the ball on the T. Well, now in the new model, the kickoff units way up ahead at the 40 yard line. There's nobody there to be able to hold the ball. So, the intent of the rule was if the ball blew off the tee twice and you needed somebody to hold it on the tee, you would then bring in your punter as the 12th player, he would hold it on the tea and then run off the field. I think, hey, we should probably find a way from a common sense standpoint to interpret the the rule the way that it was intended to be. If they there's a little bit of language that wasn't written legally, right, I think we could all probably find a way to have a little bit better interpretation and send that out in a memo. But um I don't know that anybody's asking my opinion. >> Well, I did, so that's cool. Thank you. >> That's all we've got for you, Mace. Thanks for your time.

title: Jets Fall to Lions: Glass Half Full or Empty? + O-Line & Special Teams Concerns
text: The Jets fall to the Lions and are now one and two on the season. The Jets Collective is live to break it all down. It starts right now. The Jets Collective is live. text: gutsy 49ers wins over the decade that Kyle Shanahan has been the head coach. This one might have been near the very top of the list. Insane injury attrition and the 49ers were placed completely behind the eight ball in terms of exhaustion even outside of injuries with the way that this game was going. And they found a way to win and they are now three and 0 and I'll tell you, you know, 36-30 over Arizona the final score here at Levi's Stadium. Shout out to the guys in the engineering room. Look, we've got Bill Walsh up on one of the banners above us. But you know, there's going to be so much to dig through over the course of this week with injuries. Mike Evans by the way, sounds like he's got a rib strain which is really painful. So, we'll see if he's able to come back sooner rather than later. We'll check on the the statuses of so many 49ers who dropped in this game. 49ers have problems, but every team in the NFL has problems. The 49ers get to tackle their problems with a 3 and 0 record and with the MVP favorite at quarterback. And yes, Brock Purdy is the best quarterback in football. He's the MVP favorite. I think, you know, who cares about the betting odds? I'm just talking about who the best player at the most important position is and you saw that out on the field today. Even with guys dropping like flies and that included Mike Evans who what is the fourth primary receiver to go down for the 49ers this year? Brock Purdy found a way to push through for San Francisco and it got really, really hairy there at the end because Arizona, there was a point in this game when they had run almost 30 more plays than the 49ers. So, those of you who are familiar with some of the history in 2024, hot day here at Levi's Stadium. It was like 102° down on the field. 49ers were ahead by 10 points, but they blew the lead because Arizona had controlled the game and the 49ers were exhausted down the stretch. Today, some stuff started happening that was trending against San Francisco. To the point where they had nearly 30 more Arizona had nearly 30 more plays. The 49ers were exhausted. They're down six of their top 10 defensive linemen. They need to shorten the game, not lengthen it, and Arizona was lengthening it. They had twice as much possession. The 49ers without those receivers in the second half after Evans had exited with an injury. Their Trent Williams who suffered a stinger had been carted off the field. The 49ers just needed to dig deep and possess the football. Shorthanded possess the football. Toss out the game plan that you had at the start with Mike Evans and company. You wanted it to be more explosive. You can't do that once you're down a few guys. You have to find a way to make it work with less. And that's exactly what Brock Purdy did coming out of halftime on the 58-yard touchdown drive. That's exactly what he did on that huge drive in the fourth quarter when uh he he ended up delivering the George Kittle over the middle and uh you know, several plays. They paired down the offense. They went to the day one installation and Purdy just made it work with with what he had and and it wasn't a whole heck of a lot at that point. And he did it again because the Cardinals just wouldn't go away against the exhausted 49ers defense. He did it again in the final drive that sealed it. 49ers actually made a massive massive mistake on that drive when they ran a pass play and it was incomplete with more than 2 minutes to go and basically saved Arizona from using a timeout. Well, thankfully, Christian McCaffrey decided to put the team on his back on the very next snap and rumbled carrying like seven or eight defenders on his back for about 10 yards. It was a 12-yard gain for the first down and then Purdy, of course, had the the long touchdown run which got called back by the George Kittle holding penalty, but then he found Kittle. So, Kittle essentially earned himself a touchdown by committing the holding penalty. Still a 35-yard run for Brock Purdy, something that should solidify his early lead in that MVP conversation. The guy is absolutely insane. And then you look at the fact that Christian McCaffrey would not let this team lose. You look at the fact that Deebo Samuel would not let this team lose. Those were two of the remaining skill position weapons at the end who got the ball and just turned into you know, it was a rhinoceros type of run from Christian McCaffrey. It was Deebo Samuel like a battering ram moving forward against the defense on the drive prior to that. When the going gets tough, you've got to dig into your DNA. You've got to dig into the star players, the future Hall of Famers, and Christian McCaffrey is is one of them. Brock Purdy could be on that trajectory as well if he continues delivering this. I mean, his efficiency today was off the charts again. His lead in QBR and EPA and everything over every other quarterback in the league is is only going to balloon. But you you lean into the guys who have won you so many big games, who have earned so many gutsy wins. I mean, last year they were so hurt and they won 13 games. You lean into that DNA in a game like today. So, the 49ers, they get to deal with their problems at 3 and 0. A win's a win. Today was a battle of attrition. It was warm out there. Guys were dropping. Now we get to go to the locker room and talk to Kyle Shanahan and figure out exactly what the what the 49ers injury toll is, how they're going to pick up the pieces to play the Denver Broncos next week. But I can tell you that winning a division game is never easy, even if you are fully stocked. And the 49ers today found a way to get it done despite the odds really starting to tilt against them. And one thing that you look for early in the season is what kind of character is a team going to show? Cuz there are going to be some games where everything lines up and you just blow the opponent out. There are going to be other games where that's not going to be the case. Stuff is going to work against you. So, Arizona today was running the same playbook as the Miami Dolphins did last week. They were able to shorten the game. They're running the football. We knew that they were going to have some success in that regard because the 49ers were down their top six or six of their top 10 defensive linemen. We knew all you know, that was going to be a challenge. And the 49ers, I think they they didn't run the football nearly enough in the first half. They only had seven runs. And then, you know, when Mike Evans went down, that means you lose your ex-receiver, all of a sudden that cushion that the 49ers had that I've been talking about for weeks, the spacing on the field disappeared. All of a sudden that explosive game plan which was possible when Evans was there taking defenders with him was no longer on the table. And the 49ers looked up and they weren't all that far ahead of Arizona. And Arizona had run more plays, so the 49ers defense was on pace to tire itself out. And you said, "Well, boy, the 49ers need to recalibrate here. They need to show some toughness. They need to dig deep, change the game plan, and work with what they now have." And that's where the reestablishment of the run game came came in. And we saw obviously the the epic run from Christian McCaffrey late in this game. But also, when he decided to go, you know, full LT over the over the goal line for for the touchdown. What was it? The second-to-last or third-to-last touchdown for the 49ers in the second half. I mean, they put up 36 points despite uh missing a lot of guys offensively. So, the run game came back, the short passing game came back. I mean, Purdy was just nails. So, obviously did not turn the ball over. He still has not been sacked through three games. And they finished this one with Vedarian Lowe, the swing tackle, playing at left tackle for the 49ers after Trent Williams exited with a stinger. Another injury that we've got to keep an eye out for is Dre Greenlaw. He exited this game with a quad injury. And we know that he dealt with a quad issue in Denver last season. So, uh you know, special teams today, this was its worst performance of the year for the 49ers. They muffed a punt that opened the door for Arizona late, so Purdy and the offense had to overcome that. Eddie Pinero missed two extra points. It's wild to me that Eddie's I'm going to do the math on this, so tune in when I we have the show later. Eddie has probably almost an identical career field goal percentage and extra point percentage. Like his field goal percentage entering this game was 89%, which is the second highest of all time. His extra point percentage was only 91%. So, he misses a lot of extra points and it almost cost the 49ers today, but they they got through it because they've got Mr. Purdy who, you know, you watch him and there's he's like Drew Brees, but he can run, you know, and I don't want to say Steve Young because Steve Young was arguably the greatest running quarterback of of all time, but Brock Purdy, in case you didn't notice, he's he's ultra ultra athletic. There's a reason why he's the best in the game. And just look back in the first quarter that throw to Luke Farrell when he's rolling out, flushed out of the pocket, and he jump throws at the at the sideline, and somehow he gets it to Farrell, and they say that he was barely out of bounds, and I just wish the 49ers would have challenged so we could see that play on replay a few more times. The the people who say that Brock Purdy is somehow limited athletically, they're probably three quarterbacks in the entire league who can even sniff making the throw that he made to Luke Farrell, the one near the sideline. There's nobody in the entire league outside of Purdy who hasn't been sacked yet, and that's even with the 49ers playing a backup left tackle. Like you just can't get to this guy. He led the league in pressure to sack ratio last year, and he worked with a skeleton crew last year and still finished number two in QBR. So, he's now actually working with more with Deebo Samuel and George Kittle back, and he's taking from the experience of last year when so many guys got hurt and he made it work against the division rival in the Arizona Cardinals today. The uh Seattle Seahawks lost today. Okay? So, I when I talk about teams, everybody having problems, the Seahawks have problems, too. They lost to QB2 of Washington, Marcus Mariota, and some backup offensive lineman. The Seahawks have to deal with their problems at two and one. 49ers get to deal with their problems at three and 0. I'm going to go to the locker room and find out exactly where things stand for all of these injuries. Of course, the Nick Bosa loss affected the 49ers today, but I have to say on that defensive side of the ball, and Mike, if you can type whatever you're sending me again because you I can't see beyond one line, so I only saw the first line. So, Mike, whatever you send me, please send me in uh multiple messages and and get that first line up there. But, the defensive side of the ball for the 49ers today, they absolutely strained. [snorts] And they made some plays. They got some hits in, but I knew that they weren't going to be able to seal this game when I saw that Arizona's play count in the fourth quarter was above 70 on a warm day without your closer like Nick Bosa. You still have to shout out to the plays that guys like Keion White made. And then you think about MyCole Walker. He's going to come back in week five. That's going to allow White to rush from the inside much more often, and White, he can rush from the inside. Keion White is somebody who the 49ers won't working against guards. You look at some of the plays that Fred Warner made today. Deommodore Lenoir exited for the concussion protocol, came back after he cleared it. Good thing the 49ers have such good corners and such good cornerback depth because they really needed it today. On a day where they had to manufacture the pass rush. Fred Warner was playing pass rusher earlier in this game. That I'd never had seen the 49ers rush six on a third and 15 until today. And that's what Raheem Morris is going to have to do as long as they're dealing with some of the saturation up front. Brock Purdy now has nine touchdowns through his first three games, which ties Steve Young we just talked about for the franchise record. Brock Purdy is one of the most athletic quarterbacks in all football. He's definitely the most efficient. He's a master from the pocket. There's a reason why he's the best quarterback in the game and it's because he can deliver from the pocket as he did today. He can do more with less. The 49ers were down all these weapons, down Mike Evans who obviously was featured part of the game plan. Six of Purdy's first 15 throws while Evans was in the game targeted Mike Evans. We can talk about the touchdown pass that he threw to Mike Evans that he couldn't have run up and placed and handed it to Mike Evans in a better spot. And then, you know, what was awesome about that is Evans is such a savvy vet. So, he knows that the corner is not looking for the ball, don't reach for the ball until the ball is right there because the corner is not going to know the ball's coming. So, he outfoxed the cornerback and he just, you know, plucked his arms out, plucked the ball out of the air right when it came there. But perfect pass, perfect execution. As I've said, adding Mike Evans to the 49ers offense with Brock Purdy is essentially a cheat code. Another cheat code is having Deebo Samuel as a gadget weapon and this was probably that the highlight reel play of the game, right? It seems like such a long time ago because this was such a wild 36 to 30 ride, but early in this football game the 49ers faced a third and long and they ran a hook and lateral. You have five eligibles on these plays, okay? So, five receivers who are eligible to catch a pass. Deebo Samuel was the fifth eligible on the hook and lateral. They threw it to Mike Evans and the defense converged on Mike Evans. Everybody thought, well, this must just be a hook to Mike Evans. They're giving up on third down. The fact that Deebo Samuel was not lined up as one of the featured wide receivers for the 49ers on the play meant that he went unnoticed and meant that he was able to pick up a full head of steam behind Mike Evans. And we saw Mike Evans beautiful pitch by the way as he was being dragged to the ground, pitched it to Deebo Samuel and there is probably nothing scarier for a light defensive back in the NFL than Deebo Samuel, especially in good shape right now, running with a full head of steam. Nobody wanted to get in his way and he ran away from the defense. Perfectly executed. You credit Kyle Shanahan, but also credit guys like Jordan Watkins who made a really nice catch today, made a couple really nice catches today including the one before halftime that earned the 49ers the field goal, the long one, the 50-plus yarder from Robbie Gould. Watkins active for the first time today, plays the Z. He's trusted on that seam route for Brock Purdy early. If Watkins does not have Purdy's trust, he's not playing one of those primary wide receivers positions. And the downstream effect of that is that Deebo Samuel can't just be lined up as a gadget weapon ready to pounce, ready to strike where there's opportunity. So, Watkins' contribution essentially and and the trust the 49ers have in him enables the 49ers to run that hook and lateral to Deebo Samuel early in the game and obviously who's the right man at the right time. And then later in the game Deebo Samuel turns into a bulldozer and then later in the game George Kittle gets in on it with two touchdowns and then throws the ball into the crowd. You lean on your stars and your future Hall of Famers when the going gets tough. You show the resilience of a team that can win a Super Bowl. The reason that the 49ers should be the Super Bowl favorites right now is not because oh, they got a bunch of guys hurt and and you're just trying to pretend that those injuries didn't happen. No, they have to fight week in week out. We'll see how the injury situation evolves. Of course, you need some luck over the course of the year, but the one thing that you can't teach that a lot of teams wish they had beyond just pure talent and we know the 49ers had that is gutsiness and resilience. Last year's 49ers team showed it. They won 13 games despite fielding a JV roster for much of the season. So they had this cultural resilience. They had the quarterback in Brock Purdy. Mac Jones gets a lot of credit, too. They found a way to will themselves to those 13 wins. I think a lot of that cultural resilience has now carried over into 2026 and we saw so much of it on display today. You should always be worried if you're a 49ers fan and maybe that magic won't carry over into 2026. Today was an indication that this team can win when a lot of things are stacked up against it. And again, Arizona 30 more plays, nearly 30 more plays in the second half. They were the much fresher team. Because of that, they had exhaustion on the 49ers side. They had momentum. The 49ers needed to change their plan midway because guys were getting hurt. They didn't have that separation, but they have the quarterback. They have the play caller. They have George Kittle. They have Deebo Samuel. They have Christian McCaffrey bowling through defenders. They made it work. It was going to have to be an offense-driven game. It obviously was when they went 36-30. The defense, just enough. And the special teams, unfortunately today, it was tough sledding for the 49ers on that defensive that special team side of the ball. Eddie Piniero's got to make those extra points in games like this or else they're going to get way hairier than they should be. And the Saran Neal muff punt uh that was brutal for the 49ers. It opened door for Arizona. The good news is that the first 2 weeks the special teams have been really good. So at this point you can look at it as an outlier for the 49ers. You know what's not an outlier? How damn good Brock Purdy and this entire San Francisco offense is. These guys are special. They're able to churn over 30 points even despite the the 49ers the fewest plays losing yardage by any team through 3 games in NFL history. The fewest plays losing it. They have four plays that have lost yardage over three games, the fewest in NFL history. That is a Kyle Shanahan stat, that is a Brock Purdy stat, that is a Christian McCaffrey stat, that is an O-line stat, that is an elite offense stat. And it even if the defense is leaking oil with some of these injuries and no Bosa, and they hope to get him back sooner rather than later. And we can talk about trades all we want. If Purdy is your quarterback, the MVP right now over this league, the most valuable player in this league, you've got a chance, even if the special teams is tripping over itself. Of course, you want it to be better than today, but they showed that resilience today in one of the gutsiest wins of the Shanahan era. And there have been a lot of gutsy ones, as I said at the top. All right, I am headed to the 49ers locker room. So, we will talk to you all very, very soon. Here from the Levi's Stadium engineering room, 49ers 36, Arizona Cardinals 30. 49ers in sole possession of first place in NFC West. The Seahawks lose, the Rams, the Broncos are playing now. We will talk to you very soon. Thank

And do you anticipate that either Julian Love or Taio will be able to practice this week? Thank you. >> Guys played good football. They communicated. Um there's some opportunities out there that I I think both would say that uh we'd like to be able to take advantage of next time. Uh as far as Julian goes, uh it's a day-to-day thing right now. Bob. >> Um, yeah, Mike, just when it with the your offensive running game yesterday, how much of it I guess you do look at was Washington's a really good defense versus things you guys could have done better and then just with Jadarian as well, when you looked at his his fumble, just kind of what you saw there and what's the teaching point there? >> Uh, it's both. Um, credit to Washington did a great job. Uh, and also we feel like there's plenty of room to grow. So I think it's a function of um in real time execution and also finding solutions as the game goes. Also the way the game was going of of uh some things we wanted to be able to do offensively in the pass game and in the screen game. So I think I think it's a process thing. I think we I think we stick to our process and really with like our our whole team right now and the message after the game was like I think we'd feel the same way after the game whether or not we closed it out and found a way to win or the way it the way it shook out. So, you know, really it kind of in every every tentacle from coming out of the game of where can we grow, how can we make our process better. That's been the mentality every day um or today at least. And so, and with JD, I mean um he he understands what's going on. He needs to take care of the ball. I think there's some things fundamentally where we can focus on and um we're going to continue to give him the ball. The way the game was going, you know, we needed to throw it there for the majority of the second half as well. So, um, it's probably the most not the most satisfying answer you want. I mean, I think I think there's multiple answers to it. One, hey, let's let's play better across the board. Let's get some more things. Let's let's control the game earlier in the game. So, now we can we can get to those some of those runs more so on our terms rather than be subject to to chucking around because we're we're down multiple scores in the second half. Tim. >> Hey, Mike. You mentioned this morning that you might be able to make a determination on Zack Charbanet and potentially returning him to practice. Were you guys able to decide that today? I u I mean I'm I'm in the whole Harbaugh family. I feel like I'm indebted to, you know, I just had the honor to work for for both Jim and John, obviously one year with Jim. Um, man, he he gave me so much um autonomy and like the belief that he had in our staff on defense, me me personally as well, and just like he never felt like he never left your corner, you know, and uh that meant a lot for a guy that was unproven and trying to figure things out on the fly. Understanding of like the power of you know that's really kind of like where 12 was one started to come from was like hey the power of everybody doing it together all going in the same direction. Uh the passion he had for his players. I just uh we had a blast that year in Ann Arbor and um just proud to say that I could that we work for him and and proud of the year that we had honestly.
