You know, it's including rein like what I said this morning, including reinforcing what our philosophy is on a day in dayout basis on a on a per play basis uh as a play caller, how we game plan, what's our, you know, how we get the solutions throughout games. it's uh you know how how how we play play to play as players and as a team going from unit to unit. So I think there's there's a lot of things to learn. I don't I think if you're not learning from from a game like that, you're totally missing the target. So um I'm proud of the mentality that we've had today. The guys have been um you know you can tell they're upset which they you know they should be and and uh but they're also you can you can you can feel the resolve. You can feel the the eagerness to get back at it on Wednesday. Greg, >> Mike, sorry I think I might have joined late, but your assessment of Josh Jones game yesterday at Mcfaren's pretty tough customer obviously. And then where's uh Travon Diggs and his road and his he possibly in the plans the next couple weeks? >> You ask about Josh's game? >> Yes, against in particular. Yeah, he gave up the we gave up the one nine ball, inside release nineball. Um, look, that it's it's the NFL. Um, McLaren's a great player. We're going to continue to put Josh in one-on-one situations. He's a great press player. He's a great corner and, you know, some sometimes you're going to give up completions. I mean, you can't you can't go undefeated. But, uh, I thought Josh played hard. He played technically sound. And, uh, there's a couple one-on- ons that he didn't win. There's also several one-on- ones that he did. So, that's uh that's life in the NFL. Um but we're going to continue to push coverage away from him sometimes. Sometimes we'll help him. It's just But we believe in him for sure. He's uh he's had a he's had a good start to the season. >> And Travon Diggs, where's he at in ramping up to being ready to play and where does he factor in the next couple >> Uh he's definitely definitely part of the conversation. um without getting into all the details, but he's done a great job since he got here. And uh and he's practicing well and I think uh if the situation worked out that uh you know that he could be up, I think he'd be ready to play. >> So physically he's ramped up from not having practiced since January. That's now past, >> I think. So yeah. Okay. >> Thank you, sir. Curtis. >> Yeah, Mike. Uh, just on the defense kind of collectively yesterday, only 258 yards, three at 13, third down, average drive started, I think was the 37. Um, some so some short fields for them, still 20 plus points on the board. What did you kind of make of the overall performance from from that side of the ball when you kind of factor everything in there? Um, obviously the last drive didn't go your way and such. >> When you watch the tape, like when you think about a play style, I think our guys played incredibly hard. They played physical. Um, I thought we took a lot of shots at the ball. The ball just didn't come out. There's a couple opportunities in the pass game where maybe we could have made the ball come to life. Uh, I'm I'm I mean, I know it's kind of sounds weird coming off a loss, but our effort I'm really proud of are the way our guys played, our mentality. Um I I really I really I love our group and they uh they played really hard and um it shows you the importance of like team football and also understanding situations how we can play it better. I think that's why uh the guys are disappointed because uh there's some situations that we probably could have taken better advantage of to you know put our team in a better position to to win the game. Bob Um yeah, Micah Jackson is obviously off to a great start, basically another historical start. Um whenever a lot of people from the outside or fans or whatever when they kind of look at him having that many numbers, there's sort of the philosophical question of do you need to spread it around more just to do that or can one guy kind of carry that big of a load all the time? Do you do you think philosophically that you know is that a big deal if if one guy is is getting that many get many targets in yard? >> I think I got this question last year. Um, I forget what I said. I probably should remember. Uh, he, yeah, Jax is off to a great start. We got great players around him. The ball's going to find other guys at some point. Uh, the thing that I'm probably most I told him this today with Jax's game is I thought he blocked really well, you know, and I think I think we need to improve that from our receiver position right now is getting to the third level and getting guys blocked so we can pop some some more runs. So, um, but that's the best game Jax has had blocking in a while. If he keeps doing that, then we'll be we'll be just fine. >> Brian, >> coach, I assume you put a lot of thought into like your weekly rhythm between games and how much time you allocate for everything. Uh, so I'm just curious like how much do you just want to stick to the same allocation, the same routine every week, and how much do you take in new information to decide, hey, we got to deviate and focus a little bit more on this. How does that process work? >> Yeah, it's a good question. Uh, I would consider it like tweaks to our like we have a we have a meeting every week around noon about process. And so it's uh, you know, several several coaches and people in our building sitting around about how how we went about our business and how we want to cadence things, how we want to practice, how we get the team ready. Um, so it's it's always a conversation and we we think critically about, you know, why we do what we do and when. Um, so but so I'd consider it like we're just constantly like my dad with his golf swing, you know, like constantly tinkering to try to uh make it come to life. But that's that's really our philosophy. If the whole change is needed, we would do it. I I like to think that at least. But um at this point it's really just trying to whittle away at the at the statue until it looks like Michelangelo or until it looks like David, excuse me. >> Okay, couple more. Corbin. >> Yeah, Mike. Obviously turnovers played into the field position differential yesterday, but there also were a few kick returns that were taken back for good chunks of yardage had Jason's not getting to the landing spot. How do you feel through three weeks with where you guys are at in terms of your consistency from the special teams aspect? >> Yeah, I uh I mean to put it to put it plainly, it's um it's not good enough. Uh there's things process-wise we can improve on, but you know, and we've talked about this throughout training camp and really since we got here, but a Seahawk play needs to look like a Seahawk play, and there's there's plays on tape that uh we're not doing that. So, Um the standard is higher on special teams here. We've proven that and uh the guys will get it right, but there's definitely a sense of urgency to to make it look like us and to play our style of ball on teams. >> Is Charles potentially going to fit into that here down the line? I know that he's eligible to return here after the next >> Everybody Everybody is eligible to play on our special teams units. No one is exempt from special teams consideration. Last question, Brady. Uh >> Mike, what did you see from Nick as you guys uh you know ramped up his workload? >> Thought Nick had a good game. Um there's some really great plays. Uh and he'll continue to get better. I think I think he should be really proud of how he's approached last week mentally. I think that's one of the things to answer Brian's question is something that we want to discuss as a staff of just, you know, what what the process is every week of of how how where and how often uh he plays and so we can have a really focused um game plan because where he plays really affects the position group around him because he's playing out of really three position groups. So, um that's something we'll continue to think about and make better, but he's he's done a great job. One more. You guys have had like openings at safety with, you know, people not being available. And we haven't seen DA Anthony Bell uh play, let alone just being up on the roster. What what's keeping him from getting an opportunity? >> Uh Debbell's done a great job. Um so has Max. Felt like uh Max deserved that opportunity to to come up from the practice squad yesterday and uh but we would have we wouldn't have any problem Debbell playing for us. Be excited for him to play for us. >> Thank you everyone. and we'll see you >> All right. Thank you.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "We're Going To Go Back To Work And Get Better" | Seattle Seahawks
text: OK.  It was a tough game.  You know, our guys really tried hard.  We stuck together, but I take my hat off to Washington.  I think they had a great match.  They had a great plan.  In addition, we lost three goals, but in the NFL, games are won thanks to good situational decisions, ball control, team play and a series of successful plays. We didn't do that today.  And they did, so honor and praise to them. I think the main takeaway for our team is that when we play our best Seahawks football, we have to win, even if we lose those little internal battles throughout the game.  The difference was still two points .  We could have used the situation better to gain an advantage and close out the game, but it was a tough match, a great performance from our opponent, and we move on. Third and nine at the end, what happened on that wide- front play? They switched to a different combination against the "zero" defense, made a good choice, and we couldn't stop them. What do you think of Sam overall?  About his efforts.  I mean, four touchdowns and all that, but a couple of interceptions too. Yeah, I think it's like a microcosm of the whole game. I think our guys played selflessly. I think we did a lot of good things. On offense, I think we shot the ball relatively well, but we need to protect the ball better as an offensive team.  And we have to intercept him on defense. Why do you think we didn't show much in the running game today?  What did you see there? Honestly, I'm not sure.  They had good defense.  Ahem. I think we tried to find a solution.  I also think that the course of the second half, when the weather improved and their passing game took off , forced us to change our emphasis. Did you need to apply more pressure in the center, or did you feel like the pressure was enough? No, no, we didn't press hard enough today. They took good care of their quarterback. Ahem.  We'll look at it and see where, where we can, where we can get better, but I don't think we met our goal today in terms of quarterback play. You said that red zone play was an issue last week.  What happened to the red zone play?  What do you think about how it went today? Yeah, that's not, that's not good enough.  We , we have to be better, especially in situations of sudden change of possession in defense.  I think we'll go back to our process and see what we do, how we play well, how we develop a game plan, how we practice moments.  We will go back and look at everything to see where we can improve. How concerned are you about Price's fumbles? I think it's just this team.    It's just that if we, if we lose the ball, it ends badly. So I don't need to go back to that first fumble.  We just told him to calm down and come back to the game after the break, he'll be fine.  He will figure everything out . Everything will be fine with them. What do you think about AJ Finley and how you, you know, played without Julian and how you ... With only a few days to prepare, I think he did a great job.  He did a great job.  They did some good things operationally in terms of movement and shifts, and I felt like we were organized there on defense.  It's just a matter of executing on certain points and we'll see how we can get better.    You obviously have a lot of veterans on your team.  What gives you confidence when you look at them that you will get the right reaction afterwards?    I don't think this is something you can see just in the locker room. I just know, I know our team.  I know what they are made of. I know we're going to get back to work.  We're going to get better, and that's... our job as coaches is to look at the organization of the process, and again , it's not the outcome we want, but it's a consequence of how we approach everything, how we travel, prepare, and game plan .  So we will look into everything, actively work on correcting the mistakes and move on, everything will be fine with the guys In that play before the two-minute break, did you think they would have to put the ball in play before the two-minute warning? Hmm, no, we thought they wouldn't play the ball, but we wanted to take a timeout. Nick Bosa left the field for a while, but returned and seemed to be doing well? Um, he's okay now, yeah. Sam, overall, I know there's still more to analyze, but what do you think about the way he came back and played? Yes, he made some great playmaking moments, both timely and on long plays, so I think he did a great job.  I mean, interceptions are tough, but again , we'll analyze them, understand why we made those decisions, and see what we can do better, but overall, I think it kept us in the game, that's for sure. It was like we were in a two- point deficit mode and then immediately moved up the field. There are many positives to take away from this. The question is simply how can we operationally stay ahead of the situation ?  How can we better play takeaway?  Things in that vein. Of course, you want to make interceptions, but you know, you can't just tell the players: "Make interceptions."  So how do you create more chances for those interceptions? Well, I think we just need to find ways to be more aggressive, and we'll give our opponent credit.  They had a great plan, and I think their quarterback did a few things that helped them run the combinations well , and that's their credit. So we'll analyze this again, but really a function of how often and consistently you can put pressure on the other team and have an advantage.  And today we didn't have enough of that .  So we will become better. You haven't had to go through this in a long time .  What message can you give to the team after several losses? I think the message would be the same whether we won the game or not.    It's about how we do our jobs and how we get better.  It's actually that simple.  It's about taking on problems, finding solutions throughout the week, making sure everyone sees their share of responsibility, how we can improve it, being honest with ourselves, and giving it our best effort.  We say: go through, not around, so that's exactly what we plan to do.    Did the side judge provide an explanation for Finley's penalty on McLaurin on an incomplete third down?    Uh , no.  No. Anything else? Good.  OK.  Thank you.

title: Sam Darnold Back and Seahawks Lose on the Road to the Commanders
text: The winning streak is broken for Seattle. Sam Darnold is back, but a hungry opponent south of Seattle, they're looking to steal their first win. All of that here shortly. [music] What's up, twelves? This is the Seahawks Collective presented by Hog Media. And the Seahawks go two- one after losing their first game of the season. And this is Mike McDonald's third road loss as a head coach. Only his third road loss. We'll dive into all of uh what happened, why it happened, and now what to do as the Hawks stay home for their game Sunday against the LA Chargers. And here to give us all the info we need, our Seahawks insiders. Twinning with me tonight, Brian Mhouser, our Hawk blogger. Sorry Rob, we didn't give you uh the message on that, our friend Rob Sten from the Seahawks draft blog as well. And I know there were many times on Sunday uh where you might have been questioning what is going on. So don't lie. I know you want to use this time to ask these guys some questions that you have. They've been all over it, not only at the game, but all week. Uh, but before we get to the game, some news that really directly affects our very own Brian Nimhauser. Neil Kosla, son of the new Seahawks owners, uh, tweeted out today that the team is adding two additional mics to the press conferences. And I'm assuming one of these will be pointed towards the reporter. So, Rob, I got to ask you, how does it feel that uh, you might be able to hear Brian even more clearly now in these pressers? >> Well, obviously I'm delighted by that. Can I also give a shout out to Curtis Allen who writes for my blog who was the person who actually asked >> this was a Seahawks draft blog teamwork situation. >> I I had nothing to do with it but uh he asked the question. I know it's something that Curtis has been quite frustrated by for a while. Um so he asked the question, he got an answer and uh it'd be great, you know, if if we can hear the questions really clearly in future and uh and hear the answers as well. Amazing. So well done to Curtis. What a start. >> Well, there you go. All the credit goes to Rob's team. Brian, do you think now that you'll be like more miked up, you're going to have like a little glam routine or maybe a little more meticulous on the OOTD fit? I know it might not be the camera, but just the mic. >> Uh, uh, no. I mean, the the this has been one of the funnier things to experience from both sides. So I have listened to Seahawks press conferences for decade plus whatever way back to the early you know first Pete Carol days and it was always frustrating but you had to kind of okay based on the answer I think this was the question and you kind of make it out and you go along with it but there are some fans that I just give a ton of credit to because they just continue to just scream about like can you just mic up the press so we can hear the question like we love this team so much that we listen to every press conference. Like we we don't even trust the reporters to tell us what's going on. We want to hear it for ourselves. But part of that experience is knowing what the quest [ __ ] is. So I I totally Curtis was a representative of many many fans that that have had this complaint. And we'll see. Like I think what Neil said was that they're going to have two mics. And I think that's good. I don't think that the problem is in the the the team meeting room where where the Mike McDonald and typical press conferences are happening. It happens in the indoor practice facility where it's a little more cavernous and the mic setup is not quite as good. So, tomorrow I think it'll go well. We'll see if we get to like Friday and also Thursday. The coordinators, those are the test cases where it's a little bit more challenging. And I've talked to the guys. I mean, not just the guys, the guys and gals that work in the building and they know this is a complaint. It's not quite as easy to fix as people might think. So, we we'll see. I'm really hopeful uh that that this is kicks it over the edge, but um I'm a little bit wait and see, too. >> Yeah, that uh that indoor that dang indoor, >> you know, how big it is given the audio issues. But Rob, what has it been like for you just even from afar to be able to see the new ownership be so responsive to fans in so quickly? >> Well, it's it's great. You know, the the thing that I just hope doesn't happen because I have experienced this in this country is that when owners are very active on social media, if things don't go well, they just get bombarded with stuff all of the time. And I don't think that's a healthy thing. And fans just can't help themselves. they'll just chuck in a an an account, you know, they'll put the ads of the username in the in the tweet and there and then that stuff can get a bit heavy and a bit too much sometimes. So, we'll see if that happens. Fingers crossed everything just goes peachy for the next few months and that that's never going to happen. But great to see, you know, they're they're trying to to make the experience better for the fan in this instance and I'm sure they will look for other ways to do that. And also, I'm sure behind the scenes there's a lot going on to try and make things better for the team. So, uh, if they could somehow work it for the owners to prevent the Seahawks ever having three turnovers and turning them into 21 points to the opponents in future, that would also be great as well. >> That would be great as well. But it is great kind of seeing like a friendly banter over something casual like like audio issues. And Rob, you mentioned um just the way that it goes on the response, but Brian, you really getting the reply or an ask from the fans, but Brian's getting some of the replies as well from ownership. You mean venode during the game? Is that the one you're referring to? >> Agree. Agree. >> Yeah. I have to admit so like during the especially the during the games when I'm in the press box on the road I and I'm just tweeting and like paying attention I don't really read replies and so I didn't know until I got home that night that Venode had responded. And for folks that didn't see, I thought it was I think it's ridiculous when first of all when they called a catch to Terry McLaren where he was just clearly not in. I was like, "What is going on?" And then Mike McDonald throws the challenge flag before the ref even gets under the hood to review it. They're like, "It has been overturned." And I'm like, "If it's that obvious that it was that clear, the coach, the team should get their flag but their challenge back." Like, that's just ridiculous. That's a bad rule. Um, it's basically like a failed replay um that that they should have caught themselves. And so I tweeted that and then Venode [laughter] says like agree and I'm like cool. I mean it's great >> on all your next tweets from the next games I'm just going to hit you with agree agree disagree agree >> AB I would be just as excited or disappointed depending on your replies or Rob's replies or almost anybody's replies. I I think it's cool. I think it's Venode and Neil. They're new Seahawks fans. They're obviously a key part of what's going on. I am happy to get to know them and interact with them. But I've gotten to know and interact with a lot of really cool people. Um just because you have a lot of money and you own the team does not make you more important in my mind. But uh I do really value it. Like I think it's cool that they that they're making a real effort to interact. I hope it remains positive. Um, this was the first test, you know, of what will be other tests in the future when the game doesn't go exactly the way you want it to go. So, uh, yeah, it's it's kind of fun. It's kind of a fresh fresh new experience and they seem to be having a great time and, you know, I'm enjoying watching them kind of have the time of their lives. That's I think that's pretty cool. >> It is. It is kind of cool. And I think the lesson learned is that twelves, if you got something to say, say it kindly over social media. and you very well may hear from the number ones in charge. Uh but let's do a deep dive into the details of what actually happened during Seattle's trip to Washington and their 31 to33 loss. Uh and we'll zoom we'll zoom out to start of the whole season just so far. Rob, when you've sat on this game now, like what's your overall takeaway from Sunday's game? [snorts] >> Uh just massive disappointment. I think uh that I I I woke up on Sunday and it never even crossed my mind that the Seahawks are going to lose this game. So maybe that's me. I I should have a different approach to that. I don't know. I just I'd never considered for a second that they were going to lose. It's It's not just the players who were missing who were inactive for that game. It's the players who were already out for the Washington Commanders. The quarterback obviously was missing. Uh Leo Chanel really said what happened to him. I interviewed him before the draft and really cool guy. So I was really disappointed to see that. Uh and I just thought that one way or another, even if there was going to be some adversity in this game, the Seahawks were not going to lose to the Washington Commanders. And they did. and and just there were issues, you know, the the what happened with Jarian Price, [sighs] the fact that Rasheed Shahed was anonymous again pretty much from a couple of moments, the the turnovers leading to 21 points. And I just sat there and every single series that the Commanders had, I was convincing myself, this is going to be the moment when the defense turns the ball over for the Seahawks, like this is when the swing's going to happen. And it just never came. And then even at the end that you've got two opportunities on third and long to get the ball back to your offense and at least have that chance. And I always feel like there's something really unsatisfying in football when you're watching your team and the you don't end the game with possession of the football that you don't even have that opportunity to try and march down there. If they got the ball back and they couldn't get into field goal range or Meers misses the kick, I think I would have been able to accept I still would have been really annoyed by what had happened, but I think I would have accepted it a bit more than them running to the outside with a running back who was basically unemployed for about three weeks into free agency and then Marcus Mariota doing the same thing on the next third down. I just found that particularly irritating and I thought after a couple of sleeps I would have just moved on from this and and looked ahead and and actually everything's worked against that. I then had to watch the Niners just hold on against the Cardinals and I found that very frustrating then. So the fact that the Niners are 3 and 0 annoyed me because the Seahawks aren't. And then the fact that the Rams lost again annoyed me again because then I'm thinking this was a missed opportunity to put further daylight between yourselves and the Rams which I think this is the time. >> I heard Brian was actually celebrating that but yeah, you can get mad about that too if you want. >> But this they're going through a gauntlet of games right now and your schedule is going to get harder down the line. So I think that the the wins that you get now while they're struggling and they're without Miles Garrett and Puka and they're losing games that feels important. This felt like a really big frustrating missed opportunity and um I'm I'm going to need another game to get another win and to to use this as a pallet cleanser after that. I'm afraid. >> Rob, I'll use a word that I think only when you use it on this show it holds more weight. It's peculiar. And I don't know if my accent was great, but like that's kind of how it felt. Like it was peculiar like on like that was just a peculiar game. It was a strange game. But Ryan or Brian, I bet for you you're standing in the rain postgame in a stadium called Northwest Stadium in Washington recording a postgame show on a game that none of us really thought would go the way that it did. How was that experience for you? you know, it just it didn't feel like it had been so long since they had had a loss, but it had like it's almost a year and it was also a road game in Los Angeles and LA. A lot of things about that franchise are not my favorite and they didn't even let us on the field after that for postgame. So, I had to go scramble and go somewhere into the stands and and do it there. But um it it this didn't feel like that loss and it didn't feel like any of the losses last year. It didn't feel like the Niners loss. It didn't feel like the Rams loss. It didn't feel like the Tampa Bay loss. This felt like the kind of like back when Pete Carol was the coach and they were like amazing. They almost every year would have one loss where you're like what on earth? Like how did you lose to that Jeff Fischer Rams team that was like seven and nine? like you guys are like one of the best teams ever or like they just had those. And Mike McDonald, the only other time I think he's really had one of those is against the Giants in his first season, like the fifth game or something like that. It was it was very early on. And so that this one felt like, man, why why the amount of things that they had to do wrong and that the commanders had to do right in order to lose this game was astounding. And it doesn't take more than to say like three turnovers, no takeaways, you lose that game every every single time. The Seahawks lost by two points. And all of the underlying metrics to this game make it that much more sickening. like the the Seahawks yardage advantage, the Seahawks success rate or EPA or any of the advanced metrics, they had such a massive advantage that teams that have the advantages that they have win 90 plus% of the time. So they just I mean to go on the goal line and not be able to convert, turn it over on downs, to give up touchdowns to a just absolutely mediocre to very very bad offense, you know, with a backup quarter like this just shouldn't have been. And so it is going to be a problem unless unless they go out and they just win every game like they they win they have to win the games that that maybe that they don't that you won't always expect. Maybe they win both games against the Rams instead of splitting one. Maybe they win both games against the 49ers instead of splitting. >> But I think to use a Mike McDonaldism, you got to make it right. You make a mistake, you do something wrong. happens to everybody, but don't do it again. Go out and make it right. And and they they got to do it. The starts this weekend. The Chargers are coming into town with the their tails between their legs, but they're 0 and three. And if you don't think that a Jim Harbaugh team is going to give you everything they've got this weekend, I got another thing coming for you. Like it's going to be a battle. And Rob, for you, like Brian's mentioning kind of what this has looked like for the Seahawks, having certain games like this that totally went the other way in in the past, but like when you zoom out already, how could this type of a loss affect the Seahawks in the long run for the season? I I don't think this in isolation will affect them for the but it's it's if they have a bad performance on Sunday and then it's backto back bad performances and then you've got the niners coming up all of a sudden the pressure's on a little bit and people will start asking a few questions. So uh it's amazing how things quickly can turn uh because I remember sort of thinking after the Cardinals game like this is unbelievable like this this team is is I I maybe they're just going to go on a huge tear. they're just going to dominate and they're going to get back to the Super Bowl and everything and then we had all the fuss about the Mike McDonald clip on on X last week and then you have this and it feels like it's been a bit of a crap week frankly and um I quite like to go back to how I felt seven days ago or or eight days ago. So, uh the best way to do that is to win, but there are issues, you know, we're seeing issues with the team. the running game at the moment is a huge question mark and how they deal with Janarian Price and how Jinarian Price is performing as a first round pick is a big question mark. Uh how Rasheed Shahed is, you know, involved in the offense is a question mark because he he they need to find a way to get more from him and he needs to to deliver as well. I I I think we'll come on to it later on. I still think you need more. The numbers will suggest that the pass rush was decent. I don't think that was the eye test result though and and I think you need more from the edge and I and I'm wondering how you do that frankly as well. So I think there are things that you look at after a loss if they could just go and comfortably handle the charges this weekend be feeling a lot better. But as Brian quite rightly points out this is a Harour team. I don't think they're going to have any quit in them. I I imagine that there's I can't imagine the Chargers are just going to be 0 and nine. I know they've got a very tough run that there's going to be they're going to win one of these games is basically what I'm saying that they're probably going to be underdogs in. Make sure it's not against you this weekend. All right. Well, Brian, why don't we uh solve those question marks that Rob got to not not just one, but all of them. Uh, but real quick before we do that, we're going to get to an awesome opportunity that you should hear about from our friends at SeatGeek. Hey y'all. title: Postgame Press Conference: 49ers’ Brock Purdy, HC Kyle Shanahan & more on 36-30 win over Cardinals
text: All right, guys. Um, injuries from the game. Um, Demo left, got evaluated for a concussion. He returned. Uh, Mike Evans ribs/oblique. Um, did not return. Tren Williams, stinger, did not return. Renardo Green, same thing as Deemo. Um, cleared for concussion evaluation, returned. Grayson Halden, cramps, did not return. Greenlaw, quad, um, and came back from one play, then we shut him down. Uh, Gary Wallow, stinger, he returned. Go ahead. >> Do you know the the nature of Evans rij injury? Is Is that a broken rib? >> We're not sure yet. >> Could you tell when when he did that? Was that a couple plays before he came off? >> Um I'm not No, I'm not sure when he did it. Yeah. >> I know you're concentrating on just winning this game, but as these players are going down, it seemed like almost every other play. Do you just like start thinking what's going on here? Obviously, there's other injuries going into this game. >> Uh no. I mean, you're just thinking about how to adjust and um when you lose guys, you know, especially guys like Mike and stuff, you know, changes stuff on your call sheet, changes wristbands, things like that. So, um you don't have time to think about anything else. So, when guys go down, you hope they return, but you you adjust and you wait till they tell you they're back, and if they don't, you keep it moving. Kyle, >> how many reps did you guys get this week on that on that flea flicker? >> Um just a walk through rep. Um the lateral? >> Yes. >> It's not really a flea flicker. I don't know what it is. It's a It's a lateral similar >> Yeah. >> It's crazy when Debo has zero catches but has 80 yards reception. [snorts] Um yeah, but we um it was awesome. Great ball by Brock. Great job by Mike to catch it clean. He took a hit as he was tossing it to Debo and um that's what Debo does best. He finishes and scores. >> Kyler, you you're not not known as the biggest like trick play guy and you tend to save them for big moments and big games. Why? Why that moment? >> Um, we've done that play a number of times. I don't I don't think it's that big of a trick play. You know, guys around the league do it a lot. It sounds real crazy, but just the right time. We did a couple times last year. Um, some something we've done probably four times last two years. >> When they did third and long, best chance to get it was third and long. his best chance to we knew you can't throw over throw over everybody at that time and we hoped everyone would suck up on Mike and toss it to Debo. >> When the Cardinals closes to within one, score this your second to last possession. You got to go length of the field. You started off with a couple passes with Brock, they you score the touchdown, they come back, you get another possession, couple passes by Brock. I mean, a lot of times you wouldn't want to be throwing it there. How comfortable are you now with Brock just, hey, at any time, doesn't matter if we need to burn the clock, whatever, we know move the ball, we're going to have him throw it. >> Yeah, I mean, I'm very comfortable with Brock um throwing the ball and I feel like I've always been, you know, with him, you know, in that situation, just with the timeouts they had and, you know, after us missing those extra points, I didn't look at it as a um they only needed two there on the second to on the last one, so I didn't really look at it as a just run the clock out. you know, if we go three and out, whether we're running the clock or not, I feel like they're in really good situation to go kick a field goal for the win. Uh, might have been different if they needed more than that, but I almost looked at it as normal football. It was good to soften them up with a couple passes, then we got our runs going. Um, thought it was such a huge run on second and 10. Um, we ran an inside zone to Christian. Um, I couldn't see exactly what happened, but I thought it got stuffed for like four yards. So, it's a huge third and six, I'm thinking. But, he kept his feet and we kept pushing the pile and I think he ended up getting like a 12- yard run on it, which felt like almost the biggest play of the day. >> Earlier this week, you said how Brock Party has been in so many different situations at this point that he's pretty much seasoned in understanding what to do next. He had the big scramble for the touchdown, they call it back, and then he gets it to KD for a touchdown to seal this one up. Is that an example of what you were talking about earlier this week? Um I guess I mean or and not really. I mean he just runs every play. Um he um we had a high low on his long scramble and he got flushed from the pocket. Not sure exactly why. Um and then he just made a play scrambling which I was I was looking at the passes so I was wondering why the ball wasn't in the air then he was running and the fact that he scored on that was just an unbelievable play. Joke with KD ruined that moment for him. Um and then um it was awesome job on the keeper. We ran that verse Miami in his first game I remember on a third and one and he threw it to the low guy um and missed a big touchdown over the top and that could be experience right there. Um cuz they had the low guy um might have been able to force it to him to get a couple yards um but he ended up looking over him and saw KD uncovered and got a big touchdown. >> Should KD have uh tried to get out of like taken? >> Yes, but it's on me. I didn't remind him in the huddle. I don't expect him to be paying attention to the clock. So, but I definitely wish I did um the play before that. >> Few guys stepping up today. Jordan, >> a few guys stepping up today. Jordan Watkins being one of them. What did you see from his play and what he was able to execute today? Um yeah, a bunch of guys stepped up um you know all week, you know, losing some of those receivers and then losing Mike in the game um between um walk-ins and cowing and Hodgej just having to not just go in there make the plays that you guys saw, but having to mix up their positions, move them around, just the studying that that that goes into a week to get ready to play and then when someone gets hurt have to go to a different position and be ready for that, too. So all those guys worked their butts off all week. I was really pumped for Watkins. you know, that was such a big seam route that he ran on third down. Um, you know, and he almost looked like he was going to break those tackles and score. I thought he looked real impressive on it. And then at the end of the second quarter, uh, he was the reason we got three points there on that 59 yard field goal right before the half. >> Why do you think the defense is having a tough time getting off the field? Is it just a function of the injuries? >> I mean, this No, there's always, it depends on each play and there's a couple third downs I thought we could have got off the field that we didn't. Um, there was a couple times I thought we had the quarterback, then he got away from us. Um, Brousette is seen him do that before. He's very hard to bring down. Um, you know, yeah, we got a lot of guys out there. It's um, you know, I know everyone knows the big challenge for the D line this week. You know, just losing six out of our 10 in the last two weeks, having a bunch of new guys out there and then them having to go 81 plays. [snorts] Um, which a lot of that was self-inflicted. Some was them doing some good things, too. Um, but I'm just happy how they grind and kept the Arizona out of the end zone the whole first half. Um, which I thought was a hell of a job and found a way to win at the end. >> Was the hook and ladder part of your openers? >> No. >> Uh, okay. >> Is it always like up available for each game? >> Not not always, but it was one of was one of our top calls on third and 12 plus in that section. >> I know you don't like to ask comparisons here, but I'll try. Is there any quarterback in football right now playing better than Brock Birdie? Um, I mean, I'd be surprised, but I mean, I don't study the other quarterbacks right now, so I don't really know what anyone else is doing except for the guys that we go against, so I don't get to see any of that. But, I mean, I think it's really hard to play much better than he's playing right now. >> You say he runs everything. This means everything's on the table with him. Is that basically what you're >> No, I just mean um I mean, you run the play that's called and and and if one's covered, you go to two to three to four. If you can't do that and there's open spots in the pocket instead of just taking a sack, can you make a play with your legs? Um it's he's very good at doing his job um extremely consistently. That's why I don't watch him much. I watch coverages and where the ball's going to go and he gets it there 90% of the time. uh if he didn't um it's usually because something happened that he couldn't avoid and then I look back and sometimes when see when that happens and he's running around making a play and doesn't even matter that it didn't work out because um he makes an off schedule or moves the chains with his legs. >> Eddie obviously very good on on field goals, extra points maybe a little different. Just how do you kind of view like how do you reconcile those two things when you're evaluating him? >> Uh I don't know really. I mean, I just go off of whether they made it or missed it. And um I thought that 59 yard field goal he made at the end of the second quarter was one of the biggest kicks I've seen. I mean, for us to get down there and have a chance to kick it that far with whatever we had, I think there's 20 seconds maybe on the clock, maybe 17 when we started. Um I mean, it was such a big time kick and especially for us to open it in the third quarter and have a chance to lap him, which we did. Um and I was going to probably give him a gamble or something, but he ruined that with the two extra points missed. So, >> what was your message to the team in the post game? >> Um, just I was proud of the guys, you know. I think our first two games, I don't think we had to play four quarters. Um, I thought we were ready to, but just the way the game went, you know. Um, we didn't, and that was a game that we needed to play all four quarters. That team fought to the end. Um, we were by no means perfect. We gave them some chances to get back in when I thought we could have put them away. Um, just certain mistakes, things that we can do better at. Um, but I was just proud of the guys, how they kept competing, the defense being out there for 81 plays and losing guys throughout the game and guys just keep grinding and going and I was really um, pumped with how efficient the offense was. >> Have you noticed Debo Samuel evolve or maybe approach his craft a little bit differently at this point in his career than when he was last year? >> Um, I mean I mean Debo's I think Dbo is so similar to not much different at all than when he was here last time. Um you know, we've been that's play has been installed I think for like three years now. And so finally getting it called was pretty like that's like an end of the game play. But um running on that third and long, I mean everybody's going to expect us to throw the ball to Mike Evans. So that was cool. But the unsung hero really is Luke Ferrell. Um he got out there, blocked the corner, and gave uh Debo the the edge, and then Debo just outran everybody. So Debo had an awesome statline, didn't he? Yeah, he can do it all. Wide back, whatever it is. I love Debo. He's incredible. >> Debo look like how he looked back in when he had the 1400 yard season. >> He looks great, doesn't he? >> I mean, [snorts] you know, I think all Debo needed was uh play with the boys again. Uh you know, we drafted him. Like we all love Debo. all of his best friends are here. So, uh I think that just kind of when you play with people that you really care about, it elevates your level of play. >> Said earlier when he was in here that he got to show the speed that everybody thinks he doesn't have anymore. Do do you get the sense from him that he's a little motivated by people kind of kicking dirt on his career? >> I mean, Debo's a hell of a football player and he has all the superstar tendencies like he can break off an 80 yard, he can, you know, he can take a swing pass for 80 yards. like he can do all the really cool stuff and then when you do that a lot, people just expect you to do it all the time. So then when you don't do it, people like, "Oh wow, you're slow. You're old. You're not the same guy you were anymore." And no, he just needs the opportunity to do it on a team that, you know, knows what his talents are. And I think Kyle knows exactly who Debo is. And I also I mean Debo looks fantastic. Um he's put in so much extra work. Like every Tuesday he goes on like mile jogs around the stadium. And so you guys can ask him about that, but like every Tuesday, you know, I do a workout and I see him, he goes out there in running shoes with a couple other wide receivers and they take off along the trails. Don't stalk him, please, guys. That would be so weird. But like he's putting in so much extra work just to, you know, be able to be fast, be ready, be in shape, all those things. And I mean, that's what you saw today. >> Mentioned him benefiting being back with some of his best friends. What's it been like for you guys to have him back in the locker room and his personality? I mean, Debo's just like when you put like Trent and Debo together, it's just like an a giant aura field and it just like boosts everybody's excuse me, it boosts everybody's confidence. And playing with a guy like Debo, it's just like I said, like he has all the superstar tendencies to be able to go out there and score from anywhere, break all the tackles, set the tone, and um he's he's become a really unselfish player, too. Like he doesn't care what his role is as long as the boys are doing a good job. So, we love having Debo back.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (September 29) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: All right, go ahead, >> Mike. Um, I know it was a walkth through yesterday, but Joey listed as a full participant for the first time. You expect him to play? Does that mean he will play? >> Uh, we hope so. Uh, you know, today's another day. We have a, you know, full full slot here. Obviously, we're on a Thursday Thursday schedule, so this will be more of a jog through. So, we'll have a little more pace and pretty much similar amount of reps. Um, so yeah, we see see how he does today. >> Do you need him to be a full participant today in order to feel more comfortable about him playing that first night? Well, I I think he's, you know, Joey's just like anybody else that's, you know, coming back and yeah, we want to make sure he gets everything he needs and make sure we're coordinated. >> If he does play, will he be in full or there be any kind of a pitch counter? >> That's really what the week will, you know, I you know, obviously not tomorrow will be the first time we really get to go full speed. Uh, just the way the practice structure is. So, and we'll clearly take in all the information and um and then we'll make those decisions. How would his possible unclosion kind of affect the way you guys want to play defense with him being such a good press name guy? >> Uh, great question, but I think we have to get to the game to answer it, right? So, respectfully, >> I know Jaylen and and Brandon were both limited at the swap corners. Is it hard to take a guy who's mostly been practicing outside and put him in there or is that something that's possible? >> Yeah, no, it's possible. Uh, you know, I think that's why you go back to camp and just see all the different We talk about playing different combinations, playing inside, outside. Um, but yeah, I mean, you get to the game plan aspect of it. Matchups are are a big part of it. And, you know, that's why you have the different personnel groups that get in and out of. So, um, and that's and that's that's what we're looking at because we're on a short week. Uh, we have some guys that are that are working through some things. uh the injury report, you know, we'll get get that out to everybody here, you know, after after we work. But, uh, as far as Mike, the information I was given this morning was that it really everybody was making progress. So, uh, hopefully we'll have everybody Thursday. >> Mike, you have a little bit of an unconventional schedule today with things being later. What was the process and shifting things back? Is this how you've always done it for Thursday nights? >> Uh, this is a schedule I've kind of I've grown into over the years. Um just having the opportunity to to play a number of games on Thursday. Um the the delayed start has been is very beneficial on on a number of fronts. Uh most importantly just the the ability for the players to have extra time to sleep in. Uh there's some things you know there to build into the morning as far as you know their self-care and things to get back. Um so also helps the coaches to get all the game planning done because today is really kind of a combination of Thursday and Friday. Uh so we have to have everything in for today's today's work. So there's a there's a number of factors that have led up to uh going going with a later start on the second day. So it's uh it's been very beneficial. >> What did you see from Maxi Honcho last week from a preparation standpoint that allowed him to look as composed as he did in his first start? >> Um you know I I think I think things come very natural to Max. You know obviously his experience level is what it is. you know, based off we know his history and how much he he played in college and so forth, but uh he's a gifted athlete. Obviously, he's very gifted, not athletically, but he's a powerful man. So, uh I just think it's important for us to just be in tune uh with where he is, you know, as far as his experience level. Uh that's something that uh we we is part of our game planning, you know, going up to going up to Cleveland. We anticipate a very a very loud environment. Uh so but we want to make sure that you know the pre the pre- snap for our offense that we're we're doing the things necessary to to have a healthy um pre-nap operation and you know when you have a first year player uh that that's part of that's part of the reasoning behind it. >> Mike, are you seeing some snapshots of vintage Deshawn Watson when you're watching some of the tape? >> Yeah, definitely. Uh you know Deshawn is has played some great football in his career. Just remember when he came out I mean just a dynamic player. So, it's good to see him healthy. You know, he's he's been through a lot and uh he's played some really good ball. >> After uh after the Patriots game, you talked about maybe dialing back the volume a little bit. At the same time, we saw some new wrinkles from this offense. Can you just speak to I guess maybe pairing things back, but at the same time maintaining that creativity? I think something that I've always uh held on to, you know, as a coach, you you have experience of working with others and you develop your, you know, set of coaching principles and, you know, one I've always uh leaned on for for quite some time is less volume, more creativity. Uh, you know, I'm the I'm the volume police and so I'm the bad guy and uh when it comes to those type of conversations. Uh, so it's in but it's it's it's part of your job as a head coach. So, uh, so I I think it's important to, you know, when when you say cut back, people think you're just going to line up in a, you know, in a 2 by two and a 3x3. That's not necessarily the case. And then you're definitely challenged on a short week like this, too. So, I think just trying to find a balance there as far as, you know, what we're going to do, but more importantly, how much we're going to do. It's because where we are on offense. You know, we're we don't have a ton of experience working together. So, it's uh it's important for us to, you know, be productive. You know, score more points than any other team. Uh but in the same breath, you have to grow and and you don't you know doing doing a bunch of you know a bunch of things not so well is is is in my opinion is not the best the best path to do that. >> Mike, not only have you had success on Thursday nights, but so has Aaron. He's actually tied with Dak for second most wins on Thursdays. Just what do you see from Aaron as far as his preparation or the way that he plays in some of those prime time games that have helped him have so much success? >> Well, I mean number one, I think it speaks to the level of player he is. I think you can never, you know, not start with that. But, you know, he has a lot of experience. I mean, he's played, he's played in a lot of big games and, you know, he's over 20 years of football and I always just look at the number of snaps that he's played. But, you know, to play in big games, especially play on on the road, you know, obviously in his time in Green Bay, you know, the the Thursday game was was over there in Detroit. So there's an away experience in a very very loud uh stadium and and that'll be similar to what we're going to compete in Thursday in Cleveland. So I think just drawing from those experiences um you know an ability not only to to have it yourself but share it with others. So I mean he'll be you know he he'll be a key asset for us as far as how we'll operate in the noise and he's got a ton of experience with that. >> Two more these games tend to be very physical and chippy. You could say the same for Steelers Bengals. Did you see an increase in in physicality and urgency that way on Sunday and expect that to continue? >> Yeah, I thought the game Sunday was exactly the way it was supposed to be. It was a division a division rivalry type game, you know, AFC North type football game. Uh but I'm old. I remember the 70s. I you know I I remember the Steelers and the Browns from the from those days and and I you know and I can identify with that. So yeah, we you know it's AFC North. Uh we we have three rival opponents that go through and this we we'd look for this to be a knockdown dragout type game. You guys have been pretty explosive from under center, especially last week. What's allowed you guys to to get that under center and the heavier action line? >> Uh, frankly, we're just we're just getting through our menu. You know, we we haven't we haven't played a lot of offense, frankly. I mean, we haven't been over 70 plays in a game yet. So, um, you know, our our struggles on offense were more third down in weeks one and two. And and obviously when you have that, you're you don't get as many opportunities on first and second down. So, you saw the the first down uh production go up last week and obviously the third down production was there. So, just frankly, I think we're just getting through getting through some concepts that we've been working

title: Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 4 at Cleveland Browns) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Good afternoon everyone and welcome to the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex here on the south side of Pittsburgh. Bob Pompiani flanked by Missy Matthews coming off a Steeler win yesterday and it was an impressive one 30 to27. They beat the previously undefeated Cincinnati Bengals and they did so with an offense that scored more than one touchdown in the first quarter for the first time in a long time. And Rogers was outstanding in that quarter. Right off the bat, four plays in the end zone. Roman Wilson scores, they get it back, they score another touchdown. Ben Scaranic, who knew that he was going to be involved and he was. Nice beginning and it just carried to the end of the game. Yeah, it's crazy when you think about the fact 30 points yesterday in weeks one and two only 23 combined uh for the Steelers. And it was good to see that the offense felt like it was balanced. You saw the run, you saw Jaylen Warren, an amazing performance by him, most yards from scrimmage in his career. The fact that he was battling a shoulder injury and still able to do that was great. And in terms of the defense, you did see them make the plays when they had to. Derek Harmon of course and Sebastian Joseph Day uh recovering that fumble. It was almost the perfect ending because even Jamar Chase said after the game, we were very confident we were just going to go down there and score our points and win the game and they made sure that did not happen. >> Yeah, I mean they had the ball and they were actually in field goal territory when they decided to get a little greedier and went after, you know, a pass play that Derek Harman completely blew up and they win that game. Uh, and yes, it was one of those games where you have to start with the offensive line. And this, by the way, is the Mike McCarthy press conference brought to you by PNC. We're expecting Mike McCarthy anytime here to begin his press conference every Monday at 3 p.m. on KDK Plus and Steeler Digital platforms. But the offensive line made some major changes. And when that happens, you normally don't know what to expect, especially with a rookie like Maxi Honor. But boy, he looked like a 5-year veteran in there. And Brock Hoffman obviously has some experience in the league, and that combination worked well. >> Yeah. Brock said throughout the week just working with Max someone it was the combination Mike McCarthy worked with with offensive lineman throughout the offseason and training camp. Those two were always together and Brock said he just had that look in his eyes. I knew he was going to go out there and do really big things and it was great to see. It makes me wonder were those guys supposed to be there from the beginning? Was it just because Max got injured and kind of hampered his development during the end of training camp and missing so much preseason game time? Um but it was you know risky. you move two pieces on your offensive line, but they really did a great job knowing the defense that they went against. The Bengals definitely upgraded themselves um from what we have previously seen from that unit. >> Anytime you have Dexter Lawrence in the middle, that's a handful to deal with, but and they maybe improve, but I think the Steelers found out they had the ability to move the ball on them and they did. And you know, when you're talking about the offensive line, for Aaron Rogers to do what he can do and still at his age can do, which is zip the ball all over the place, make right reads, put the ball in in tight windows, that offensive line has to be good. They ran the ball to the left. I thought Fatano McCormack did a very good job. Anytime Darno Washington helps as a lead blocker, [clears throat] that's always like bowling ball, you know, watching it go down the alley and knock over pins. >> But Rogers has to have that protection to be effective. Well, and he had the most time to throw yesterday than he has in his entire career going back to last season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. And then there was Joe Burrow who is getting it out as quick as humanly possible because that's the only way you can stop the Steelers pass rush and the guys that he knows are used to taking him down. >> Yeah, I think Roger's at 3.19 seconds, which is an eternity based on what he's been in the past afforded. Uh, and as you know, if you told me Missy that the Steelers would get no sacks until the final play of the game essentially, I would have said, "Well, that's not a good recipe here, that's the Steel when they've had success against Joe Burrow, they put pressure. They've sacked him multiple times in games. They made interceptions, picked sixes, but because of pressure, they didn't really get that much pressure. To your point, it was about them getting the ball out quickly." >> Yeah, they wanted to avoid that uh disaster that typically happens whenever Joe Burrow is facing the Steelers defense. They just seem to have his number. But don't forget Joe Burrow came into this game at 3 and one at Ara Stadium. Uh so it's not like he [snorts] hasn't done it before and I think we were all scared it was going to unfortunately happen again at the end. But I do think in terms of the Steelers defense, they were doing everything they could to try to get to him. But when you're throwing it that quickly, there's really not much you can do. >> You know, we talk about special teams a lot. Um Danny Crossman will speak here later in this hour, I'm sure. you you have to make plays on special teams. And the Steelers hit all their field goals, but they came up with two big plays. One was well, actually it was Cincinnati bad plays. They punted only twice, >> but they took advantage. >> They took advantage of it. They turned it into points. 10 points, I think, to be exact. So, uh, when Cedric Johnson comes in and roughs Cameron Johnston, I mean, if you're Zack Taylor, you got to be saying, "What are you doing? We're getting the ball. We just forced a three and out or whatever it was." And then Keshan Williams, a former Steeler, all he has to do is catch the ball. And beyond that, the guy who was right next to him, all he had to do is fall on it. I have no idea why guys want to pick the ball up, especially in that situation. >> Correct. I mean, Brandon Eckles was right there. You just saw when I saw it live, I didn't know what exactly happened, but you see just dink off of his helmet. Uh Brandon Eckles unfortunately did get hurt on that play and wasn't able to return to the game. But Ben Scronic, there's a reason why he was a Pro Bowler last season. He's just one of those gritty guys. Arthur Smith called him scroll dirt just because that's just how he plays and he's gritty and I don't think anybody had, you know, any thought in their mind that when Ben Scronic went to recover that fumble, he wasn't going to be the one that came up with it. >> He always gets down there first and he had a big part of the offense, too. Uh they sequenced a play in which you think he's going to be a lead blocker for maybe Jaylen Warren and then he takes off, gets behind the defense. Rogers put it right there. Later they ran that same play only this time he was blocking. So that's the whole beauty of play calling. I think Mike McCarthy did a very good job. >> Yeah. And that was similar to what they did last year when Ben Scrronic got the first touchdown of the season in New York. He was more the Calvin Austin guy. Uh when they had four touchdowns in that game, which was crazy, but yeah, it was good to see Ben get involved. It kept people, you know, a little uneven because when you're scouting the Steelers at this point, if you see Ben Scronicanin, you're probably assuming a run, right? Right. Um so it did help on in terms of that. And also I think just you know again the offense getting going distributing the ball by Aaron Rogers to multiple weapons was good to see and good for everybody. Roman Wilson finding the end zone DK Metaf all things you want to see want to see them continue to build on >> the Metaf one was interesting because two Bengals collided and I think that crisscross kind of messed them up but two guys were wide. Michael Yeah. So uh that kind of stuff is good to see using the middle of the field cross patterns all that kind of stuff. It's interesting now the Steelers won, but so did the Baltimore Ravens last night and so did the Cleveland Browns. And so that leads us to all four teams being two and one in the AFC North with a showdown coming up in Cleveland and >> on a short week. >> On a short week and you'd like to get a win here if you're the Steelers just because it hasn't happened in so long on Thursday Night Football and it's a big one right now. >> Yes, they have not won on Thursday Night Football on the road since 2007. That was against the St. Louis Rams for the kids who don't know that. That's what they used. >> That was the Willie Parker game where he got injured. Yep. Is that right? >> Yep. We had a uh you and I had to look that one up. But we'll give credit to Alec, one of our video guys who knew that. But it just seems that every year they play in Cleveland on Thursday night. Last year was in Cincinnati and it just doesn't go well. 0 and seven against division opponents on the road on Thursday night for >> I will say this though, Missy, it's not the dead of winter when you have - 8 degrees and snow, right? So this is a different time. Maybe that's going to work for the Steelers advantage. >> That is true. And you have to think too, different coaching staff. How is coach McCarthy going to approach the short week? Will it help that it's earlier in the season? I I don't know. We're going to get a chance to hear from him in a little bit, which is good just to see his process because I cannot imagine what guys like Jaylen Warren feel like today knowing that you're going to go play another game in a very short period of time. I think you know across the board players don't love Thursday night games. Aaron Rogers called Jaylen Warren one of the toughest guys he's ever played with and that was on display this week where he had that shoulder injury and that's never easy. He gets through that game but now short week you wonder what it's going to feel like when he woke up today. So, and they're going to count on him. Why not? He's been their best runner, >> right? And you have to, you know, is Rico healthy? Uh will he be able to be back in ter in terms of the running back rotation? And if he is, how will they do that now knowing what Jaylen Warren was able to do as the featured back? So, a lot of uh questions. I'm sure Mike McCarthy might not have all the answers today just because you are quickly turning the page thinking about the Browns, but again, also have to clean house. Clean up some things in the house is what he was using last week in terms of the things they need to fix. >> Mike McCarthy press conference brought to you by PNC. Here's Mike McCarthy. >> What you see that um what is it that stands out about Jaylen? I know you know when you look back at the film, what did you see so special about >> Jayen Warren? >> Yeah, I'm sorry. Uh Jaylen Warren had a uh excellent excellent day. Uh received the game ball, the offensive game ball, uh his production, but uh I think the thing that consistently impresses me about Jaylen among other things is his uh yards after contact. I think his ability to, you know, just keep going. Uh stays on his feet and, you know, tough I mean tough tough football player, but uh he was big for us yesterday. when when you're making decisions about splitting carries in the back field, how do you balance keeping guys fresh throughout games and healthy throughout seasons with also maybe riding the hot hand and giving a guy who's producing well more carries? >> You know, I think that's all that's all part of it. We do a playtime report uh on Fridays, you know, with the coordinators. We have a coordinator meeting [snorts] uh at the end of the day on Fridays. We go through the, you know, the projected [clears throat] 48 49 players uh for the roster. And that's when you have those conversations. So, and you try not to, you know, you try not to sway from that too much, but sometimes the game takes you takes you in that direction. So, and I think uh just the way the game was and you know, we anticipated, you know, scoring points and, you know, how many points um so that was that was really part of him playing as much as he did. How about the play of Zack Frasier with everything he had on his plate, captain and the challenge across from him Sunday? >> I thought Zach took a big step not only as a, you know, performer as far as his performance, but you know, as a captain and, you know, I thought he did a nice job open up his his heart and his teammates. You can see, you know, how much his teammates appreciate him and it's it's a big part of why we do weekly captains. you know, it's it's an opportunity for three individuals on a weekly basis uh to to be in that role and um and it's, you know, so far it's it's been neat to see uh you know, the group of players cuz obviously I don't know them that way and and so and I think you know growth and development emotionally, mentally and is very important to the development of your team. You know, we talk so much about, you know, what their physical physical abilities are and and judge about, you know, what what they've done on the field, but creating opportunities for for for these for these men to grow and express themsel is is is is a big part of why I do that. So, and um I thought I thought, you know, Zach did did a nice job with it this week. >> You've won you've won a lot of games on on Thursdays throughout your uh coaching career. Um do you >> Thank you for noticing. I now now I don't have to look it up because I made that statement then after I earlier to a group of people and and I thought well I might want to check that to make sure I was as successful as I thought I was. But what was the record? I'm just curious. >> I think 16 and six. >> Okay. >> Thanks Bert. [laughter] But when you have a record like that on on Thursdays, I know obviously being in the same division as the Lions and then coaching the Cowboys, you play on Thanksgiving and things like that, but over the over that many times, what have you learned about the prep during these kind of weeks that's led to that successful? >> Well, I I think the reality of it is, you know, every one of those games was different, but I think the fact is just from a planning perspective, you've been in, you know, so many of them. So uh I think preparation in season is is is a big part of you know you know surviving and thriving on the ride of this journey that that happens each and every week. Uh so um I think we have a good schedule. We have a we have a good thought process. Uh we we adjust in the areas we feel like we need to adjust. We'll do the same this week. [snorts] You know we're still in the midst of the preparations right now. You know we haven't we haven't had our practice yet today. you know, a walk through actually. So, um I just think we have a sound plan. I think we pay attention to the things that are most important and uh in tune with in environment that we need to play in too. So, I mean playing on the road on Thursday is a lot different obviously than playing at home. So, um but I think the fact that we're close, I think that that's that helps. Um um you know, it's just a bus ride up there. But, you know, we actually even had a conversation yesterday about sleeping in your own bed, you know, just because the importance of sleep and so forth and feel to realize you you know, you have to be there at least 19 hours before the game. So, that's not going to happen. But, you know, just just my point is looking at every every part of the of the the Thursday schedule just to make sure we're doing what's best for the players. Back along those lines, I know you haven't had a ton of time to look at it yet, but Cleveland, how [cough and clears throat] are they getting around Miles not being there anymore up front and how are guys like Verse and Graham sort of stepping up both in terms of the run and the pass? >> Well, I think Graham obviously, you know, jumps off the tape at you and and I think, you know, the Dline as a whole. Verse, you know, I had a chance to see him live in the practice opportunities against the Rams, you know, when I was out there in California. Sam Williams, someone I've coached, we drafted him out of Old Miss. So, uh, they're playing really good def, you know, team defense. Um, you know, it's a different system, you know, from, you know, Jim Schwarz when he was there. So, we're just, you know, looking at those changes. Um, you know, just just on the fact that we just played Cincinnati where you're able to watch the tape of the games last year versus Pittsburgh and see the same system on defense but just different players where now you're seeing the same players but different system. So just working through that as far as our offense versus our defense. So um but it's a very talented football team. They're playing with a lot of confidence. Uh you can see that in their wins. So we're looking forward to Thursday night football. I mean it's going to be it's incredible. I mean Thursday night I've never not experienced in an atmosphere that you you would you love to compete in. And it'll be that way when we get to Cleveland. So um it's it's going to be a battle. It's the Steelers versus the Browns. We know what that means. So, you know, I grew up with that and I'm looking forward to playing in my first Pittsburgh Cleveland football game. >> When we talked to Aaron, he talked about the scoring touchdown and how you guys had a look, dual look of a run and a pass based off of that, but you flipped it was uh from doing the pass first instead of the run first. Was that based off of a rushing success that you guys had had? And what goes into your game planning and making a call like that in the middle of the game? Well, I I think you know, a lot of those things is you you have a plan and and you you want to fit as fit as many of the runs to the passes as possible, whether it's ingame or the prior game. And, you know, that's why they they call it selfcott and that's why you do it. Uh the ingame frankly is the most important. And I think you just got to give credit to the players and coaches, the communication on the sideline of, you know, and and and that's what it's about. I I've I've always done it that way. You know, even as far as, you know, running inside zone versus outside zone and and Zach was going to the Zach questions, you know, just communication Zach had given us on, you know, how it was going inside and how he felt, you know, with the the big tackles of, you know, the the the block the combination blocks that we were doing. So, I mean, that's that's just a real credit to the coaches and players that the [snorts] the communication that's given and and then, you know, then when you do call it, it works. It's, you know, it's really a product of everybody involved. >> Darnell had a Darnell had another big catch and run where he's dragging guys, running through guys. What goes through your mind when he's on one of those runs and you're watching from the sideline? >> Why don't you give him the ball more? I think that's probably what everybody else is saying. But, um, yeah. Uh, he's he's he's unique. Um, you could just you can see and it seems like it's always on the sideline. It just people just you get, you know, he's a hard guy to tackle. I mean, he's he's a tough matchup. Um, he's done [snorts] an incredible job. Uh, you know, I always want to praise him because I I know how important it is to him, but I know how important he has been to to our football team. You know, when you're a new coach, you put in a new system, new operation, program, how you operate, and guys like Darnell that are here every day, that that means the world. And uh, he's been that guy. So, it's no surprise to me to see him continue to have success because he puts the work in. What is maybe the most surprising thing about his skill set now that you've worked with him? >> Oh my god. I mean, I just I think to be, you know, at that size and, [clears throat] you know, his body comp and what he's able to do. Yeah. And, you know, he's got natural hands.
